Makkiyya (Meccan).

{1–3} He, exalted is He, informs us about His Great Book, and that it is sent down and revealed from Allah, the One worthy of worship (al-ma'luh al-ma'bud), for His perfection and His being singular in His actions. {Al-'Aziz} (the Mighty): He who, by His might, has subdued every creature. {Al-'Alim} (the All-Knowing): of everything. {Ghafir al-dhanb} (Forgiver of sin): toward those who commit sins. {Qabil al-tawb} (Accepter of repentance): from those who repent. {Shadid al-'iqab} (Severe in punishment): against those who dare to commit sins and do not repent from them. {Dhi al-tawl}: that is, bounty and comprehensive kindness. When He had established what He established of His perfection, and this necessitated that He alone be the one worthy of worship, to whom works are made sincere, He said: {There is no god but He; to Him is the final return}.

The connection between mentioning the revelation of the Qur'an from God, described with these attributes, is that these attributes entail all the meanings the Qur'an contains. The Qur'an is either: news about God's names, attributes and actions, and these are names, attributes and actions. Or it is news about past and future unseen matters; these are from the teaching of the All-Knowing to His servants. Or it is news about His great blessings and abundant favours, and the commands that lead to them; this is indicated by His saying {Dhi al-tawl}. Or it is news about His severe retribution and what necessitates and calls for it of disobedience; this is indicated by His saying {Shadid al-'iqab}. Or it is a call to sinners to repentance, turning back to Him and seeking forgiveness; this is indicated by His saying {Ghafir al-dhanb wa qabil al-tawb shadid al-'iqab}. Or it is news that He alone is the one worthy of worship and the one who is worshipped, and the establishment of rational and transmitted proofs for this, and exhortation to it, and prohibition of worshipping other than God, and the establishment of rational and transmitted proofs for the corruption of that, and warning against it; this is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: {There is no god but He}. Or it is news about His just judgement of recompense, the reward of the good-doers and the punishment of the disobedient; this is indicated by His saying: {To Him is the final return}. This is all that the Qur'an contains of lofty matters.

{4} He, blessed and exalted, informs that none dispute concerning His signs except those who disbelieve. The dispute meant here is disputing to refute the signs of God and confronting them with falsehood; this is the practice of the disbelievers. As for the believers, they submit to the truth so that they may thereby crush falsehood. A person should not be deceived by the worldly condition of a human being and think that God's giving him in this world is evidence of His love for him and that he is upon the truth. Hence He said: {Let not their movement throughout the lands deceive you} (i.e., their coming and going in them with various kinds of trade and gain). Rather, it is obligatory for the servant to weigh people by the truth, to look at the legal realities, and to measure people by them, and not to measure the truth by people, as is the way of one who has no knowledge and no intellect.

{5} Then He threatened those who dispute with the signs of God in order to nullify them, as those before them did among the nations: {the people of Noah} and {'Ad}, {and the factions after them}, who formed parties and gathered together against the truth to nullify it, and for falsehood to support it. And the situation reached such a point, and their factionalism led them to the point that {every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him}; i.e., to kill him. This is the utmost that can be done to the messengers, who are the leaders of the people of goodness, who possess the pure truth about which there is no doubt or ambiguity. They plotted to kill them. Is there, after this tyranny, error and wretchedness, anything but the great punishment from which they will never emerge? Hence He said, concerning their worldly and otherworldly punishment: {So I seized them}; i.e., because of their denial and their factionalism. {Then how was My punishment}: it was the most severe and dreadful punishment, being either a blast or a storm of stones sent down upon them, or a command to the earth to seize them, or to the sea to drown them. So behold, they became extinct.

{6} {Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved}; i.e., just as it was fulfilled against those, so the word of misguidance was fulfilled against them, from which arose the word of punishment. Hence He said: {That they are the companions of the Fire}.

{7} He, exalted is He, informs of the perfection of His kindness towards His believing servants, and of the means He has arranged for their felicity, from causes outside their own capacity: the seeking of forgiveness for them by the nearly-brought-near angels (al-malā'ika al-muqarrabūn), and their supplication for them with what is good for their religion and their Hereafter. Included in this is information about the nobility of the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh) and those around it, their nearness to their Lord, the abundance of their worship, and their sincere counsel to the servants of Allah, knowing that Allah loves this from them. So He said:

{Those who bear the Throne} — i.e., the Throne of the Most Merciful, which is the ceiling of created things, the greatest, widest, most beautiful, and nearest to Allah, the Exalted, which has encompassed the earth, the heavens and the Kursi (al-kursī, the footstool). These angels, Allah has entrusted them with bearing His mighty Throne; there is no doubt that they are among the greatest, most exalted and strongest of the angels. Allah's choosing them to bear His Throne, His placing them first in mention, and their nearness to Him, indicate that they are the most excellent kinds of angels, peace be upon them. Allah the Exalted said: {And above them, on that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord} (69:17).

{And those around it} — from the angels nearest in rank and excellence.

{Glorify their Lord with praise} — this is a commendation of them for the abundance of their worship of Allah, especially glorification (tasbīḥ) and praise (taḥmīd). All other acts of worship enter into the glorifying and praising of Allah, for they are a declaration of His transcendence above the servant directing them to other than Him, and a praise of Him, the Exalted. Indeed, praise (ḥamd) is itself worship of Allah, the Exalted. As for the servant's saying, "Subḥān Allāh wa-biḥamdih" (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him), it is included in this and is among the acts of worship.

{And they seek forgiveness for those who believed} — this is among the fruits and very numerous virtues of faith: that the angels, who have no sins, seek forgiveness for the people of faith. Thus the believer, by his faith, has caused himself to attain this great favour.

Since forgiveness has necessary requirements that cannot be completed without them — beyond what comes to the minds of many, that the aim of asking for it and seeking it is merely the forgiveness of sins — Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the attribute of their supplication for them for forgiveness by mentioning what it cannot be completed without, and so He said:

{Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge} — Your knowledge has encompassed everything; nothing is hidden from You, and there escapes Your knowledge not the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater. Your mercy has encompassed all things; the cosmos, its upper and lower parts, has been filled with the mercy of Allah, the Exalted, and has encompassed them, and has reached what His creation has reached.

{So forgive those who have repented} — from polytheism and sins;

{and followed Your way} — by following Your messengers, in affirming Your oneness and obeying You;

{and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire} — i.e., protect them from the punishment itself, and protect them from the causes of punishment.

{8} {Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them} — upon the tongues of Your messengers — {and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants} — i.e., those who became righteous through faith and righteous deeds; their wives and husbands, and their companions and associates. {Indeed, You, You are the Exalted in Might} — the Subduer of everything; by Your might You forgive their sins, remove from them what is feared, and bring them to every good. {the Wise} — who places things in their proper places; so we do not ask You, our Lord, for a matter which Your wisdom requires otherwise. Rather, it is from Your wisdom, which You informed of upon the tongues of Your messengers, and which Your bounty has required, that You forgive the believers.

{9} {And protect them from evil deeds} — i.e., the evil deeds and their consequences, because they harm their doer. {And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day} — i.e., the Day of Resurrection — {You have truly granted him mercy.} Because Your mercy has never ceased to be continuous upon the servants; nothing prevents it except the sins and evil deeds of the servants. So whoever You protect from evil deeds, You have granted success in good deeds and their good reward. {And that} — i.e., the removal of what is feared through the protection from evil deeds and the attainment of what is loved through the attainment of mercy — {is the great triumph} — than which there is no triumph, and the competitors do not compete for anything better than it.

This supplication from the angels includes: the perfection of their knowledge of their Lord; seeking nearness to Allah through His Beautiful Names, by which He loves His servants to seek nearness to Him; and supplicating with what suits what they ask Allah for. Since their supplication was for the attainment of mercy and the removal of the effect of what the human souls require — souls whose deficiency and demands Allah knows, which require sins and the like, and the other causes and means which Allah has comprehended in knowledge — they sought nearness through the Most Merciful, the All-Knowing. It also includes the perfection of their good manners with Allah, the Exalted, by acknowledging His lordship over them, the general and the particular, and that they have no share in the affair at all; and their supplication to their Lord proceeds from one who is poor in essence in every respect, who never boasts before his Lord in any state, for it is nothing but the bounty, generosity and kindness of Allah. It also includes their complete agreement with their Lord, by loving what He loves of deeds — which are the acts of worship they performed and strove in with the striving of lovers — and of the servants who are the believers, whom Allah the Exalted loves among His creation. The rest of the accountable creatures are hated by Allah except the believers among them. So from the angels' love for them, they supplicated to Allah and strove for the righteousness of their conditions, because supplicating for a person is among the strongest indications of love for him, since one supplicates only for someone he loves.

It also includes, in what Allah explained and detailed of their supplication — after His saying "and they seek forgiveness for those who believed" — a subtle admonition regarding how to contemplate His Book, and that the contemplator should not be limited to the bare meaning of the word alone, but should contemplate the meaning of the word; and when he understands it correctly as intended, he considers with his intellect that matter and the paths leading to it, and what it cannot be completed without, and what depends upon it; and he is certain that Allah intended it, just as he is certain that He intended the specific meaning indicated by the word. Two things make him certain that Allah intended it: first, his knowledge and certainty that it is a consequence of the meaning and dependent upon it; second, his knowledge that Allah is All-Knowing of everything, and that Allah commanded His servants to contemplate and reflect upon His Book. Allah, the Exalted, has known what follows from those meanings, and He is the One who informed that His Book is guidance, light and clarification for everything, and that it is the most eloquent of speech and the most exalted in clarification. Thereby the servant attains great knowledge and abundant good according to what Allah grants him success in.

In this our exegesis there is much of this, which Allah has bestowed upon us; and in some verses its source may be hidden from one who is not a careful reflector of sound thought. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to open for us from the treasuries of His mercy what will be a cause for the righteousness of our conditions and the conditions of the Muslims. We have no recourse but to cling to His generosity and to seek means through His kindness, in which we continually turn in every moment and every instant. And we ask Him, by His bounty, to protect us from the evil of our own souls, which prevents and obstructs the arrival of His mercy. Indeed He is the Generous, the Bestower, who bestows the means and what they cause. This includes that the companion — a spouse, a child, or a friend — is made happy by his companion, and his association with him becomes a cause of good that comes to him from outside his own deed and the cause of his deed, just as the angels supplicated for the believers and for whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and descendants. It may be said that their righteousness must exist, by His saying "and whoever is righteous"; then this would be a result of their own deeds. And Allah knows best.

All other acts of worship enter into the glorifying and praising of Allah, for they are a declaration of His transcendence above the servant directing them to other than Him, and a praise of Him, the Exalted. Indeed, praise (ḥamd) is itself worship of Allah, the Exalted. As for the servant's saying, "Subḥān Allāh wa-biḥamdih" (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him), it is included in this and is among the acts of worship.

{And they seek forgiveness for those who believed} — this is among the fruits and very numerous virtues of faith: that the angels, who have no sins, seek forgiveness for the people of faith. Thus the believer, by his faith, has caused himself to attain this great favour.

Since forgiveness has necessary requirements that cannot be completed without them — beyond what comes to the minds of many, that the aim of asking for it and seeking it is merely the forgiveness of sins — Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the attribute of their supplication for them for forgiveness by mentioning what it cannot be completed without, and so He said:

{Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge} — Your knowledge has encompassed everything; nothing is hidden from You, and there escapes Your knowledge not the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater. Your mercy has encompassed all things; the cosmos, its upper and lower parts, has been filled with the mercy of Allah, the Exalted, and has encompassed them, and has reached what His creation has reached.

{So forgive those who have repented} — from polytheism and sins;

{and followed Your way} — by following Your messengers, in affirming Your oneness and obeying You;

{and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire} — i.e., protect them from the punishment itself, and protect them from the causes of punishment.

{8} {Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them} — upon the tongues of Your messengers — {and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants} — i.e., those who became righteous through faith and righteous deeds; their wives and husbands, and their companions and associates. {Indeed, You, You are the Exalted in Might} — the Subduer of everything; by Your might You forgive their sins, remove from them what is feared, and bring them to every good. {the Wise} — who places things in their proper places; so we do not ask You, our Lord, for a matter which Your wisdom requires otherwise. Rather, it is from Your wisdom, which You informed of upon the tongues of Your messengers, and which Your bounty has required, that You forgive the believers.

{9} {And protect them from evil deeds} — i.e., the evil deeds and their consequences, because they harm their doer. {And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day} — i.e., the Day of Resurrection — {You have truly granted him mercy.} Because Your mercy has never ceased to be continuous upon the servants; nothing prevents it except the sins and evil deeds of the servants. So whoever You protect from evil deeds, You have granted success in good deeds and their good reward. {And that} — i.e., the removal of what is feared through the protection from evil deeds and the attainment of what is loved through the attainment of mercy — {is the great triumph} — than which there is no triumph, and the competitors do not compete for anything better than it.

This supplication from the angels includes: the perfection of their knowledge of their Lord; seeking nearness to Allah through His Beautiful Names, by which He loves His servants to seek nearness to Him; and supplicating with what suits what they ask Allah for. Since their supplication was for the attainment of mercy and the removal of the effect of what the human souls require — souls whose deficiency and demands Allah knows, which require sins and the like, and the other causes and means which Allah has comprehended in knowledge — they sought nearness through the Most Merciful, the All-Knowing. It also includes the perfection of their good manners with Allah, the Exalted, by acknowledging His lordship over them, the general and the particular, and that they have no share in the affair at all; and their supplication to their Lord proceeds from one who is poor in essence in every respect, who never boasts before his Lord in any state, for it is nothing but the bounty, generosity and kindness of Allah. It also includes their complete agreement with their Lord, by loving what He loves of deeds — which are the acts of worship they performed and strove in with the striving of lovers — and of the servants who are the believers, whom Allah the Exalted loves among His creation. The rest of the accountable creatures are hated by Allah except the believers among them. So from the angels' love for them, they supplicated to Allah and strove for the righteousness of their conditions, because supplicating for a person is among the strongest indications of love for him, since one supplicates only for someone he loves.

It also includes, in what Allah explained and detailed of their supplication — after His saying "and they seek forgiveness for those who believed" — a subtle admonition regarding how to contemplate His Book, and that the contemplator should not be limited to the bare meaning of the word alone, but should contemplate the meaning of the word; and when he understands it correctly as intended, he considers with his intellect that matter and the paths leading to it, and what it cannot be completed without, and what depends upon it; and he is certain that Allah intended it, just as he is certain that He intended the specific meaning indicated by the word. Two things make him certain that Allah intended it: first, his knowledge and certainty that it is a consequence of the meaning and dependent upon it; second, his knowledge that Allah is All-Knowing of everything, and that Allah commanded His servants to contemplate and reflect upon His Book. Allah, the Exalted, has known what follows from those meanings, and He is the One who informed that His Book is guidance, light and clarification for everything, and that it is the most eloquent of speech and the most exalted in clarification. Thereby the servant attains great knowledge and abundant good according to what Allah grants him success in.

In this our exegesis there is much of this, which Allah has bestowed upon us; and in some verses its source may be hidden from one who is not a careful reflector of sound thought. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to open for us from the treasuries of His mercy what will be a cause for the righteousness of our conditions and the conditions of the Muslims. We have no recourse but to cling to His generosity and to seek means through His kindness, in which we continually turn in every moment and every instant. And we ask Him, by His bounty, to protect us from the evil of our own souls, which prevents and obstructs the arrival of His mercy. Indeed He is the Generous, the Bestower, who bestows the means and what they cause. This includes that the companion — a spouse, a child, or a friend — is made happy by his companion, and his association with him becomes a cause of good that comes to him from outside his own deed and the cause of his deed, just as the angels supplicated for the believers and for whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and descendants. It may be said that their righteousness must exist, by His saying "and whoever is righteous"; then this would be a result of their own deeds. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 10–12:

{10} He, may He be exalted, informs of the disgrace and shame that will befall the disbelievers, and of their request to return and to leave the Fire, and of the impossibility of that for them, and of their rebuke. He says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾. He uses the general term to include all kinds of disbelief: disbelief in God, or in His books, or in His messengers, or in the Last Day, when they enter the Fire and acknowledge that they deserve it because of the sins and burdens they committed. So they loathe themselves for that with the utmost loathing, and become angry with themselves to the utmost degree of anger. Then they will be called, and it will be said to them: ﴿The hatred of God﴾; that is, His hatred of you when you were called to faith and you disbelieved; that is, when the messengers and their followers called you to faith and set before you the clear proofs by which the truth becomes evident, yet you disbelieved and renounced the faith for which God created you, and you departed from His vast mercy. So He hated you and was averse to you. ﴿That is greater than your hatred of yourselves﴾; that is, this hatred has continued upon you, and the displeasure of the Generous has been upon you, until your state came to what it came to. So today, the anger and punishment of God have descended upon you, while the believers have attained the good pleasure of God and His reward.

{11} So they wish to return, and ﴿they say: "Our Lord, You have made us die twice and You have given us life twice"﴾. They mean the first death, and the period between the two blowings of the Trumpet according to what has been said, or pure non-existence before their creation, then He caused them to die after He had brought them into being. ﴿And You have given us life twice﴾: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter. ﴿So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way to get out?﴾; that is, they lamented and said this, but it did not benefit them and did not avail them.

{12} They are rebuked for not having taken the means of salvation. It is said to them: ﴿That is because when God alone was invoked, you disbelieved﴾; that is, when He was called to His oneness and to sincerity in works for Him, and when association with Him was forbidden, ﴿you disbelieved﴾ in Him, and your hearts recoiled from that, and you were utterly repulsed. ﴿But when partners were associated with Him, you believed﴾; that is, this which brought you to this station and placed you in this abode and place is that you disbelieve in faith and believe in disbelief, you are content with what is evil and corrupt in this world and the Hereafter, and you dislike what is good and righteous in this world and the Hereafter. You prefer the cause of wretchedness, humiliation and anger, and you renounce what is the cause of success, prosperity and victory. ﴿And if they should see the way of right guidance, they would not adopt it as a way; but if they should see the way of error, they would adopt it as a way﴾. ﴿So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Most Great﴾. The Most High: the One who possesses absolute highness from all aspects: highness of essence, highness of rank, and highness of dominion. From the highness of His rank is the perfection of His justice, and that He places things in their proper places and does not equate the righteous with the wicked. The Most Great: the One who possesses majesty, greatness and glory in His names, attributes and actions, exempt from every defect, flaw and deficiency. Since judgment belongs to God, and He has judged against you with eternal abiding, His judgment cannot be changed or altered.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 13–17:

{13} He, the Exalted, mentions His great blessings upon His servants by making the truth distinct from falsehood, through the signs He shows them within themselves, in the horizons, and in the Qur'an, which point to every sought-after objective and clarify guidance from error. So no doubt remains for one who reflects on them and contemplates them about knowing the realities. This is among the greatest of His blessings upon His servants, for the truth has not been left ambiguous nor righteousness confused. Rather, He has varied the indications and clarified the signs, so that whoever perishes does so upon clear evidence, and whoever lives does so upon clear evidence. The more exalted and great a matter is, the more numerous and easier its proofs are. Consider tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness): since its question is among the greatest questions, indeed the greatest, the rational and transmitted proofs for it are abundant and varied. God has coined examples for it and multiplied argumentation for it. For this reason He mentions it in this place and draws attention to a number of its proofs, saying: ﴿So call upon Allah, making religion sincerely His﴾.

When He mentioned that He shows His servants His signs, He drew attention to a great sign, saying: ﴿And He sends down for you provision from the sky﴾; that is, rain, by which you and your livestock obtain sustenance and live. This indicates that all blessings come from Him. From Him are the blessings of religion, which are the religious matters, the proofs for them, and what follows from acting upon them. All worldly blessings are like the blessings that arise from the rain by which the lands and the servants come to life. This indicates with decisive clarity that He alone is the one worthy of worship, to whom sincere devotion in religion is required, just as He alone is the Bestower of blessings. ﴿And none is mindful﴾ of the signs when they are reminded of them ﴿except one who turns back﴾ to Allah, the Exalted, by turning toward His love, His fear, His obedience, and humbling himself before Him. It is this person who benefits from the signs, and they become a mercy for him, and his insight increases through them.

{14} Since the signs yield remembrance, and remembrance necessitates sincere devotion to Allah, He ordered this consequence with the fa' that indicates causation, saying: ﴿So call upon Allah, making religion sincerely His﴾. This includes both the supplication of worship and the supplication of request. Ikhlas (sincere devotion) means purifying one's intention for Allah, the Exalted, in all acts of worship, obligatory and recommended, concerning the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants. That is, be sincere to Allah, the Exalted, in everything you hold as your religion and draw near to Him through. ﴿Even if the disbelievers are averse﴾ to that. So do not care about them, and do not let that turn you away from your religion, and do not let the blame of any blamer deter you. For the disbelievers are extremely averse to sincere devotion to Allah alone, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾.

{15} Then He mentioned of His majesty and perfection that which necessitates sincere devotion to Him, saying: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Possessor of the Throne﴾; that is, the Most High, who established Himself upon the Throne and exclusively possesses it, whose degrees are raised to a height that distinguishes Him from His creation, whose rank is elevated, whose attributes are glorified, and whose essence is exalted, so that He is not drawn near to except by pure, purified, righteous deeds. This is sincere devotion, which raises the degrees of its adherents, brings them near to Him, and makes them superior to His creation. Then He mentioned His blessing upon His servants through prophethood and revelation, saying: ﴿He casts the Spirit﴾; that is, the revelation, which for the hearts and souls is like the spirit for the bodies. Just as the body without the spirit does not live or subsist, so the soul and the heart without the spirit of revelation are neither made right nor prosper. ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command﴾, which contains the benefit and welfare of the servants, ﴿upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾, namely the messengers whom He preferred and singled out for His revelation and for calling His servants.

The purpose of sending the messengers is to secure the happiness of the servants in their religion, their worldly life, and their hereafter, and to remove wretchedness from them in their religion, their worldly life, and their hereafter. For this reason He said: ﴿That he may warn﴾ (the one upon whom Allah casts the revelation) ﴿of the Day of Meeting﴾; that is, he warns the servants of it and urges them to prepare for it by the means that save them from what will occur therein. He named it the Day of Meeting because on it the Creator meets the created, the created meet one another, and the doers meet their deeds and their recompense.

{16} ﴿The Day they will come forth﴾; that is, they will be visible upon the earth, having gathered on one plain in which there is no crookedness or elevation. The caller will make them hear, and the sight will penetrate them. ﴿Nothing of them will be hidden from Allah﴾: neither their essences, nor their deeds, nor the recompense for those deeds. ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾; that is, who is the owner of that great day, which gathers the first and the last, the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, on which partnership in dominion has ceased and all means have been severed, and nothing remains but righteous or evil deeds? ﴿The dominion is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾; that is, the One who is singular in His essence, His names, His attributes, and His acts, so that He has no partner in any of them in any respect. The Subduer over all creatures, to whom the creatures have submitted, been humbled, and become subservient, especially on that day when faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting, on which no soul will speak except by His permission.

{17} ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴾ in the world, of good and evil, little and much. ﴿There is no injustice today﴾ against anyone, neither by adding to their evil deeds nor by diminishing their good deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾; that is, do not regard that day as far off, for it is coming, and everything that is coming is near. He is also swift in calling His servants to account on the Day of Resurrection, owing to the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the perfection of His power.

They were stronger than these people in number, in equipment, and in the size of their bodies, ﴿and [more]﴾ mighty ﴿in traces upon the earth﴾, in building and planting. Then he mentioned an example of the conditions of those who denied the messengers, namely Pharaoh and his soldiers, saying:

{23} That is: ﴿And We indeed sent Moses﴾, son of Imran, to the kind of these deniers, ﴿with Our signs﴾, the great signs that decisively demonstrate the truth of what he was sent with and the falsehood of what those he was sent to held, namely polytheism and what follows from it, ﴿and a clear authority﴾. That is, a manifest proof that takes hold of hearts so that they submit to it, like the staff that became a serpent and similar clear signs with which Allah strengthened Moses and enabled him to establish the truth to which he called.

{24} The ones he was sent to were ﴿Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was of the people of Moses but who oppressed them with his wealth. All of them rejected him in the strongest manner and said: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾.

{25} ﴿When he came to them with the truth from Us﴾, supported by Allah with dazzling miracles that necessitate complete submission, they did not meet it with that. Mere abandonment and aversion did not suffice them, nor even denying it and opposing it with their falsehood. Rather, their vile condition reached the point that ﴿they said: Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women. But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾. They devised this scheme, supposing that if they killed their sons, the people would not grow strong and would remain in their servitude and under their bondage. Yet their plot was ﴿only in error﴾, for what they intended did not come to pass; rather, the opposite of what they intended befell them. Allah destroyed them and annihilated them to the last one.

Principle: Reflect on this point, which frequently recurs in the Book of Allah, the Exalted: when the context concerns a particular story or a particular matter, and Allah wishes to pass a ruling on that particular matter that is not restricted to it, He states the ruling and attaches it to a general description, so that it is more comprehensive, includes the case for which the discourse was brought, and removes the misconception that the ruling is restricted to that particular matter. For this reason He did not say, "Their plot is only in error," but said: ﴿And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.

{26} ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, arrogant, tyrannical, deceiving his foolish people: ﴿Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord﴾. That is, he claimed, may Allah disfigure him, that were it not for considering the feelings of his people, he would have killed him, and that the supplication of his Lord would not prevent him. Then he mentioned what moved him to intend killing him, claiming that it was sincere advice to his people and the removal of evil from the land, so he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾, which you follow, ﴿or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾. How most astonishing this is! That the most evil of creatures should advise people against following the best of creatures. This is from the deception and propaganda that enters only the minds of those about whom Allah said: ﴿So he made his people light-headed, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people﴾.

{27} ﴿And Moses said﴾, when Pharaoh uttered that vile statement that his tyranny had compelled him to make, relying on his power and authority, while seeking refuge in his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord﴾. That is, I have taken refuge in His lordship by which He governs all affairs ﴿from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account﴾. That is, his arrogance and his failure to believe in the Day of Account carry him to evil and corruption. Pharaoh and others are included in this, as was mentioned previously in the principle. So Allah, the Exalted, protected him by His kindness from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account, and provided for him the means by which the evil of Pharaoh and his chiefs was averted from him.

{28} Among the means was this believing man from the family of Pharaoh, from the house of the kingdom. He must have had an audible word, especially since he was showing agreement with them while concealing his faith. For they usually show him consideration in a way they would not if he opposed them openly. Likewise Allah protected His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) through his uncle Abu Talib from the Quraysh, since Abu Talib was a leader among them who agreed with them in their religion. Had he been a Muslim, that protection would not have come from him. So this believing man, the one granted success, intelligent and resolute, said, denouncing the deed of his people and the monstrousness of what they had resolved: ﴿Will you kill a man merely because he says: My Lord is Allah?﴾ That is: how can you consider it lawful to kill him when his sin and crime is that he says, "My Lord is Allah"? And it was not merely a statement devoid of proofs, which is why he said: ﴿And he has certainly come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾, because his clear evidence was well known among them, so that both the young and the old knew of it. That is: this does not necessitate his killing. So why did you not first refute what he brought of the truth and confront the proof with a proof that refutes it, and then consider whether it is lawful to kill him if you prevail over him with argument or not? As for now, when his argument has become evident and his proof has prevailed, then between you and the permissibility of killing him are deserts across which the necks of camels are broken.

Then he said to them a rational statement that satisfies every intelligent person in any circumstance: ﴿And if he is a liar, his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾. That is, Moses is between two situations: either he is a liar in his claim, or he is truthful in it. If he is a liar, then his lie is upon him and its harm is limited to him, and there is no harm to you in that, since you have refrained from answering and confirming him. If he is truthful, and he has come to you with clear proofs and informed you that if you do not respond to him, Allah will punish you with a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter, then some of what he promises you will certainly befall you, namely the punishment of this world. This is from his good intellect and gentle manner in defending Moses, since he presented this answer which leaves them no confusion, and made the matter revolve around these two states. In every case, killing him is folly and ignorance on your part.

Then he moved on, may Allah be pleased with him, grant him satisfaction, forgive him and have mercy on him, to a matter higher than that and to explaining Moses' closeness to the truth, so he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor﴾, that is, one who exceeds the limit by abandoning the truth and turning to falsehood, ﴿a liar﴾, by attributing to Allah what he has transgressed in. So Allah does not guide such a person to the path of right; neither in what he indicates nor in his proof, and he is not granted success on the straight path. That is: you have seen what Moses called to of the truth and what Allah guided him to explain of the rational proofs and heavenly marvels. Whoever is guided with such guidance cannot be a transgressor or a liar. This is evidence of his perfect knowledge, intellect and recognition of his Lord.

{29} Then he warned his people, advised them, and frightened them with the punishment of the Hereafter, and forbade them from being deceived by apparent sovereignty, so he said: ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿dominant in the land﴾ over your subjects, executing whatever arrangements you wish. ﴿So who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes to us?﴾ That is, His punishment. This is from the goodness of his call, since he made the matter shared between himself and them by saying ﴿who will help us﴾ and ﴿if it comes to us﴾, so as to make them understand that he gives sincere advice to them as he gives it to himself, and wishes for them what he wishes for himself. ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, opposing him in that and deceiving his people so that they would follow Moses: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. He spoke truly in saying ﴿I show you only what I see﴾, but what did he see? He saw that he should make his people light-headed so they would follow him, in order to secure his leadership over them. He did not see the truth with him; rather he saw the truth with Moses and denied it while being certain of it. He lied in saying ﴿I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾, for this is an inversion of the truth. Had he commanded them to follow him merely in his disbelief and error, the evil would have been lighter. But he commanded them to follow him, claiming that in following him is following the truth, and in following the truth is following error.

{30} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating the call to his people, not despairing of their guidance, as is the state of those who call to Allah, the Exalted. They do not cease calling to their Lord, nor is anyone who turns them away able to stop them from repeating the call, nor does the obstinacy of those they call deter them. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾, meaning the deniers among past nations who banded together against their prophets and united to oppose them.

{31} Then he explained them, saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud and those after them﴾, that is, like their habit of disbelief and denial, and Allah's custom with them of swift punishment in this world before the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice to the servants﴾, so that He would punish them without a sin they committed or a crime they had earlier perpetrated.

{32} When he had frightened them with worldly punishments, he frightened them with the punishments of the Hereafter, so he said: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire: ﴿that we have found what our Lord promised us to be true...﴾ to the end of the verses, and ﴿the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: Pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided you. They will say: Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers﴾. And when the people of the Fire call to Malik: ﴿Let your Lord put an end to us﴾, he will say: ﴿Indeed, you will remain﴾. And when they call to their Lord: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾, He will answer them: ﴿Remain in it, and do not speak to Me﴾. And when it is said to the polytheists: ﴿Call upon your partners,﴾ so they call upon them, ﴿but they will not respond to them﴾.

{33} So he frightened them, may Allah be pleased with him, with this awesome day, and he grieved for them if they persisted in their polytheism. For this reason he said: ﴿The day you turn back fleeing﴾, that is, you will have been driven to the Fire. ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾, neither from yourselves, having any strength by which you could repel the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone besides Him help you, ﴿the day the secrets are tested. Then he will have no power and no helper﴾. ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, because guidance is in the hand of Allah, the Exalted. When He withholds guidance from His servant, knowing that he is unworthy of it because of his corruption, there is no way to guide him.

{34} ﴿And Joseph certainly came to you﴾, son of Jacob, peace be upon them both, ﴿before﴾ the coming of Moses with the clear proofs that indicate his truthfulness, and he commanded you to worship your Lord alone with no partner. ﴿But you continued in doubt about what he brought you﴾ during his lifetime. ﴿Until when he died﴾, your doubt and polytheism increased, ﴿and you said: Allah will never send after him a messenger.﴾ That is: this is your false supposition and your presumption, which is not befitting of Allah, the Exalted. He, the Exalted, does not leave His creation neglected, not commanding them and forbidding them, but sends His messengers to them. To suppose that Allah does not send a messenger is a supposition of misguidance. For this reason He said: ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whoever is a transgressor [and doubter]﴾. This is their true description, by which they described Moses with injustice and arrogance. They are the transgressors, by exceeding the truth and deviating from it into error, and they are the liars, since they attributed that to Allah and denied His messenger. Whoever is characterized by transgression and lying, and does not depart from them, Allah does not guide, nor does He grant him success in good, because he rejected the truth after it reached him and he recognized it. So his recompense is that Allah punishes him by withholding guidance from him, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, ﴿and We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

{35} Then He mentioned the description of the transgressing liar, saying: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which have made the truth distinct from falsehood and have become, in their clarity, like the sun to sight. They dispute about them despite their clarity, in order to repel and nullify them, ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, that is, without any proof or evidence. This is a necessary description of everyone who disputes concerning the signs of Allah, for it is impossible to dispute with authority, because the truth is not opposed by any opponent. It is therefore impossible to oppose it with any legal or rational proof at all. ﴿Greatly hateful is that﴾ statement which includes rejecting the truth with falsehood, ﴿in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾. Allah is most intensely hostile to its speaker, because it contains denial of the truth, affirmation of falsehood, and attributing that to Him. These are matters that intensify Allah's hatred for them and for whoever is characterized by them. Likewise, His believing servants detest them with the utmost detestation, in agreement with their Lord. These are the elite of Allah's creation, so their detestation is evidence of the vileness of those they detest. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, as He sealed the hearts of the family of Pharaoh, ﴿Allah seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾, arrogant against the truth by rejecting it, and against people by belittling them, a tyrant through his excessive injustice and aggression.

{36–37} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing Moses and denying him in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is established upon the Throne and exalted above creation: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower﴾, that is, a great elevated structure, and its purpose is: ﴿that I may reach the heavens, and look at the God of Moses, though I think him to be a liar﴾ in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens. But he wanted to take precaution and test the matter himself. Allah, the Exalted, stated what moved him to this statement: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾. So the evil deed was made attractive to him, and Satan continued to adorn it for him, calling to it and making it seem good, until he saw it as good and called to it, and debated as one who is sincere would debate, though he was among the greatest corrupters. ﴿And he was barred from the way﴾, the truth, because of the falsehood that was made attractive to him. ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴾, that is, loss and destruction, which brought him nothing but misery in this world and the Hereafter. He intended by it to plot against the truth and to make people think that he was right and that Moses was in the wrong.

{38} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating his sincere advice to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, not as Pharaoh tells you, for he will guide you only to the way of error and corruption.

{39} ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is only a enjoyment﴾, enjoyed and delighted in for a little while, then it ends and vanishes. Do not let it deceive you and mislead you away from that for which you were created. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, the place of residence and the dwelling of rest and stability. So you ought to prefer it and work for it, with deeds that will make you happy there.

{40} ﴿Whoever does an evil deed﴾, whether polytheism, grave disobedience, or sin, ﴿will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, that is, he will be recompensed only with what will harm and grieve him, because the recompense for evil is evil. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, from deeds of the heart, the limbs, and the words of the tongue, ﴿those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account﴾, that is, they will be given their reward without limit or counting, rather Allah will give them what their deeds could never reach.

{41} ﴿And O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation﴾ through what I have told you, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾ by abandoning the following of the Prophet of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him.

{42} Then he explained that, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of﴾, that it deserves to be worshipped besides Allah, and speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most abominable sins. ﴿And I call you to the Mighty﴾, who possesses all power, while others have no part in the affair at all, ﴿the Forgiving﴾, who forgives His servants who are excessive against themselves and who dare to displease Him. When they repent and turn to Him, He removes their sins and wrongs and averts their causes of worldly and otherworldly punishments.

{43} ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, truly and certainly, ﴿that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is, it does not deserve to be called to nor to be sought for refuge in this world or the Hereafter, because of its weakness and deficiency, and because it possesses neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection. ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾, the Exalted, and He will recompense every doer according to his deeds. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, those who have transgressed against themselves by daring against their Lord with His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and no others.

{44} When he had advised them, warned them and admonished them, and they neither obeyed him nor agreed with him, he said to them: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ of this advice, and you will see the consequence of not accepting it when punishment befalls you and you are deprived of the great reward. ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾; that is, I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, cast all my affairs upon Him, and rely upon Him for my welfare and for averting the harm that may befall me from you or from others. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: He knows their conditions and what they deserve. He knows my condition and my weakness, so He will keep me safe from you and suffice me against your evil, and He knows your conditions, so you do not act except by His will and His decree; if He gives you power over me, then that proceeds from His wisdom, the Exalted, and from His will and decree.

{45–46} ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾; that is, Allah, the Strong, the Merciful, shielded that believing man, who was granted success, from the punishments of what Pharaoh and his household schemed against him, namely their intention to destroy and ruin him. This was because he confronted them with what they disliked, and openly showed complete agreement with Musa (peace be upon him), calling them to what Musa had called them to. This is something they could not tolerate, and they were the ones holding power at that time. He had angered them and their rage against him intensified, so they intended to harm him, but Allah protected him from their plot and scheme, and their plot and scheme turned back upon themselves. ﴿And there befell the household of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾: Allah drowned them all, to the last of them, in a single morning, and in the barzakh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour arises, [it will be said], "Admit the household of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ These are the dreadful punishments that befall those who deny the messengers of Allah and oppose His command.

{23} That is: ﴿And We indeed sent Moses﴾, son of Imran, to the kind of these deniers, ﴿with Our signs﴾, the great signs that decisively demonstrate the truth of what he was sent with and the falsehood of what those he was sent to held, namely polytheism and what follows from it, ﴿and a clear authority﴾. That is, a manifest proof that takes hold of hearts so that they submit to it, like the staff that became a serpent and similar clear signs with which Allah strengthened Moses and enabled him to establish the truth to which he called.

{24} The ones he was sent to were ﴿Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was of the people of Moses but who oppressed them with his wealth. All of them rejected him in the strongest manner and said: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾.

{25} ﴿When he came to them with the truth from Us﴾, supported by Allah with dazzling miracles that necessitate complete submission, they did not meet it with that. Mere abandonment and aversion did not suffice them, nor even denying it and opposing it with their falsehood. Rather, their vile condition reached the point that ﴿they said: Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women. But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾. They devised this scheme, supposing that if they killed their sons, the people would not grow strong and would remain in their servitude and under their bondage. Yet their plot was ﴿only in error﴾, for what they intended did not come to pass; rather, the opposite of what they intended befell them. Allah destroyed them and annihilated them to the last one.

Principle: Reflect on this point, which frequently recurs in the Book of Allah, the Exalted: when the context concerns a particular story or a particular matter, and Allah wishes to pass a ruling on that particular matter that is not restricted to it, He states the ruling and attaches it to a general description, so that it is more comprehensive, includes the case for which the discourse was brought, and removes the misconception that the ruling is restricted to that particular matter. For this reason He did not say, "Their plot is only in error," but said: ﴿And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.
