They are the transgressors, by exceeding the truth and deviating from it into error, and they are the liars, since they attributed that to Allah and denied His messenger. Whoever is characterized by transgression and lying, and does not depart from them, Allah does not guide, nor does He grant him success in good, because he rejected the truth after it reached him and he recognized it. So his recompense is that Allah punishes him by withholding guidance from him, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, ﴿and We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

{35} Then He mentioned the description of the transgressing liar, saying: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which have made the truth distinct from falsehood and have become, in their clarity, like the sun to sight. They dispute about them despite their clarity, in order to repel and nullify them, ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, that is, without any proof or evidence. This is a necessary description of everyone who disputes concerning the signs of Allah, for it is impossible to dispute with authority, because the truth is not opposed by any opponent. It is therefore impossible to oppose it with any legal or rational proof at all. ﴿Greatly hateful is that﴾ statement which includes rejecting the truth with falsehood, ﴿in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾. Allah is most intensely hostile to its speaker, because it contains denial of the truth, affirmation of falsehood, and attributing that to Him. These are matters that intensify Allah's hatred for them and for whoever is characterized by them. Likewise, His believing servants detest them with the utmost detestation, in agreement with their Lord. These are the elite of Allah's creation, so their detestation is evidence of the vileness of those they detest. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, as He sealed the hearts of the family of Pharaoh, ﴿Allah seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾, arrogant against the truth by rejecting it, and against people by belittling them, a tyrant through his excessive injustice and aggression.

{36–37} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing Moses and denying him in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is established upon the Throne and exalted above creation: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower﴾, that is, a great elevated structure, and its purpose is: ﴿that I may reach the heavens, and look at the God of Moses, though I think him to be a liar﴾ in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens. But he wanted to take precaution and test the matter himself. Allah, the Exalted, stated what moved him to this statement: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾. So the evil deed was made attractive to him, and Satan continued to adorn it for him, calling to it and making it seem good, until he saw it as good and called to it, and debated as one who is sincere would debate, though he was among the greatest corrupters. ﴿And he was barred from the way﴾, the truth, because of the falsehood that was made attractive to him. ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴾, that is, loss and destruction, which brought him nothing but misery in this world and the Hereafter. He intended by it to plot against the truth and to make people think that he was right and that Moses was in the wrong.

{38} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating his sincere advice to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, not as Pharaoh tells you, for he will guide you only to the way of error and corruption.

{39} ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is only a enjoyment﴾, enjoyed and delighted in for a little while, then it ends and vanishes. Do not let it deceive you and mislead you away from that for which you were created. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, the place of residence and the dwelling of rest and stability. So you ought to prefer it and work for it, with deeds that will make you happy there.

{40} ﴿Whoever does an evil deed﴾, whether polytheism, grave disobedience, or sin, ﴿will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, that is, he will be recompensed only with what will harm and grieve him, because the recompense for evil is evil. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, from deeds of the heart, the limbs, and the words of the tongue, ﴿those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account﴾, that is, they will be given their reward without limit or counting, rather Allah will give them what their deeds could never reach.

{41} ﴿And O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation﴾ through what I have told you, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾ by abandoning the following of the Prophet of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him.

{42} Then he explained that, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of﴾, that it deserves to be worshipped besides Allah, and speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most abominable sins. ﴿And I call you to the Mighty﴾, who possesses all power, while others have no part in the affair at all, ﴿the Forgiving﴾, who forgives His servants who are excessive against themselves and who dare to displease Him. When they repent and turn to Him, He removes their sins and wrongs and averts their causes of worldly and otherworldly punishments.

{43} ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, truly and certainly, ﴿that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is, it does not deserve to be called to nor to be sought for refuge in this world or the Hereafter, because of its weakness and deficiency, and because it possesses neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection. ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾, the Exalted, and He will recompense every doer according to his deeds. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, those who have transgressed against themselves by daring against their Lord with His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and no others.

{44} When he had advised them, warned them and admonished them, and they neither obeyed him nor agreed with him, he said to them: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ of this advice, and you will see the consequence of not accepting it when punishment befalls you and you are deprived of the great reward. ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾; that is, I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, cast all my affairs upon Him, and rely upon Him for my welfare and for averting the harm that may befall me from you or from others. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: He knows their conditions and what they deserve. He knows my condition and my weakness, so He will keep me safe from you and suffice me against your evil, and He knows your conditions, so you do not act except by His will and His decree; if He gives you power over me, then that proceeds from His wisdom, the Exalted, and from His will and decree.

{45–46} ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾; that is, Allah, the Strong, the Merciful, shielded that believing man, who was granted success, from the punishments of what Pharaoh and his household schemed against him, namely their intention to destroy and ruin him. This was because he confronted them with what they disliked, and openly showed complete agreement with Musa (peace be upon him), calling them to what Musa had called them to. This is something they could not tolerate, and they were the ones holding power at that time. He had angered them and their rage against him intensified, so they intended to harm him, but Allah protected him from their plot and scheme, and their plot and scheme turned back upon themselves. ﴿And there befell the household of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾: Allah drowned them all, to the last of them, in a single morning, and in the barzakh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour arises, [it will be said], "Admit the household of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ These are the dreadful punishments that befall those who deny the messengers of Allah and oppose His command.

{23} That is: ﴿And We indeed sent Moses﴾, son of Imran, to the kind of these deniers, ﴿with Our signs﴾, the great signs that decisively demonstrate the truth of what he was sent with and the falsehood of what those he was sent to held, namely polytheism and what follows from it, ﴿and a clear authority﴾. That is, a manifest proof that takes hold of hearts so that they submit to it, like the staff that became a serpent and similar clear signs with which Allah strengthened Moses and enabled him to establish the truth to which he called.

{24} The ones he was sent to were ﴿Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was of the people of Moses but who oppressed them with his wealth. All of them rejected him in the strongest manner and said: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾.

{25} ﴿When he came to them with the truth from Us﴾, supported by Allah with dazzling miracles that necessitate complete submission, they did not meet it with that. Mere abandonment and aversion did not suffice them, nor even denying it and opposing it with their falsehood. Rather, their vile condition reached the point that ﴿they said: Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women. But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾. They devised this scheme, supposing that if they killed their sons, the people would not grow strong and would remain in their servitude and under their bondage. Yet their plot was ﴿only in error﴾, for what they intended did not come to pass; rather, the opposite of what they intended befell them. Allah destroyed them and annihilated them to the last one.

Principle: Reflect on this point, which frequently recurs in the Book of Allah, the Exalted: when the context concerns a particular story or a particular matter, and Allah wishes to pass a ruling on that particular matter that is not restricted to it, He states the ruling and attaches it to a general description, so that it is more comprehensive, includes the case for which the discourse was brought, and removes the misconception that the ruling is restricted to that particular matter. For this reason He did not say, "Their plot is only in error," but said: ﴿And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.

{26} ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, arrogant, tyrannical, deceiving his foolish people: ﴿Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord﴾. That is, he claimed, may Allah disfigure him, that were it not for considering the feelings of his people, he would have killed him, and that the supplication of his Lord would not prevent him. Then he mentioned what moved him to intend killing him, claiming that it was sincere advice to his people and the removal of evil from the land, so he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾, which you follow, ﴿or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾. How most astonishing this is! That the most evil of creatures should advise people against following the best of creatures. This is from the deception and propaganda that enters only the minds of those about whom Allah said: ﴿So he made his people light-headed, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people﴾.

{27} ﴿And Moses said﴾, when Pharaoh uttered that vile statement that his tyranny had compelled him to make, relying on his power and authority, while seeking refuge in his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord﴾. That is, I have taken refuge in His lordship by which He governs all affairs ﴿from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account﴾. That is, his arrogance and his failure to believe in the Day of Account carry him to evil and corruption. Pharaoh and others are included in this, as was mentioned previously in the principle. So Allah, the Exalted, protected him by His kindness from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account, and provided for him the means by which the evil of Pharaoh and his chiefs was averted from him.

{28} Among the means was this believing man from the family of Pharaoh, from the house of the kingdom. He must have had an audible word, especially since he was showing agreement with them while concealing his faith. For they usually show him consideration in a way they would not if he opposed them openly. Likewise Allah protected His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) through his uncle Abu Talib from the Quraysh, since Abu Talib was a leader among them who agreed with them in their religion. Had he been a Muslim, that protection would not have come from him. So this believing man, the one granted success, intelligent and resolute, said, denouncing the deed of his people and the monstrousness of what they had resolved: ﴿Will you kill a man merely because he says: My Lord is Allah?﴾ That is: how can you consider it lawful to kill him when his sin and crime is that he says, "My Lord is Allah"? And it was not merely a statement devoid of proofs, which is why he said: ﴿And he has certainly come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾, because his clear evidence was well known among them, so that both the young and the old knew of it. That is: this does not necessitate his killing. So why did you not first refute what he brought of the truth and confront the proof with a proof that refutes it, and then consider whether it is lawful to kill him if you prevail over him with argument or not? As for now, when his argument has become evident and his proof has prevailed, then between you and the permissibility of killing him are deserts across which the necks of camels are broken.

Then he said to them a rational statement that satisfies every intelligent person in any circumstance: ﴿And if he is a liar, his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾. That is, Moses is between two situations: either he is a liar in his claim, or he is truthful in it. If he is a liar, then his lie is upon him and its harm is limited to him, and there is no harm to you in that, since you have refrained from answering and confirming him. If he is truthful, and he has come to you with clear proofs and informed you that if you do not respond to him, Allah will punish you with a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter, then some of what he promises you will certainly befall you, namely the punishment of this world. This is from his good intellect and gentle manner in defending Moses, since he presented this answer which leaves them no confusion, and made the matter revolve around these two states. In every case, killing him is folly and ignorance on your part.

Then he moved on, may Allah be pleased with him, grant him satisfaction, forgive him and have mercy on him, to a matter higher than that and to explaining Moses' closeness to the truth, so he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor﴾, that is, one who exceeds the limit by abandoning the truth and turning to falsehood, ﴿a liar﴾, by attributing to Allah what he has transgressed in. So Allah does not guide such a person to the path of right; neither in what he indicates nor in his proof, and he is not granted success on the straight path. That is: you have seen what Moses called to of the truth and what Allah guided him to explain of the rational proofs and heavenly marvels. Whoever is guided with such guidance cannot be a transgressor or a liar. This is evidence of his perfect knowledge, intellect and recognition of his Lord.

{29} Then he warned his people, advised them, and frightened them with the punishment of the Hereafter, and forbade them from being deceived by apparent sovereignty, so he said: ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿dominant in the land﴾ over your subjects, executing whatever arrangements you wish. ﴿So who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes to us?﴾ That is, His punishment. This is from the goodness of his call, since he made the matter shared between himself and them by saying ﴿who will help us﴾ and ﴿if it comes to us﴾, so as to make them understand that he gives sincere advice to them as he gives it to himself, and wishes for them what he wishes for himself. ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, opposing him in that and deceiving his people so that they would follow Moses: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. He spoke truly in saying ﴿I show you only what I see﴾, but what did he see? He saw that he should make his people light-headed so they would follow him, in order to secure his leadership over them. He did not see the truth with him; rather he saw the truth with Moses and denied it while being certain of it. He lied in saying ﴿I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾, for this is an inversion of the truth. Had he commanded them to follow him merely in his disbelief and error, the evil would have been lighter. But he commanded them to follow him, claiming that in following him is following the truth, and in following the truth is following error.

{30} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating the call to his people, not despairing of their guidance, as is the state of those who call to Allah, the Exalted. They do not cease calling to their Lord, nor is anyone who turns them away able to stop them from repeating the call, nor does the obstinacy of those they call deter them. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾, meaning the deniers among past nations who banded together against their prophets and united to oppose them.

{31} Then he explained them, saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud and those after them﴾, that is, like their habit of disbelief and denial, and Allah's custom with them of swift punishment in this world before the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice to the servants﴾, so that He would punish them without a sin they committed or a crime they had earlier perpetrated.

{32} When he had frightened them with worldly punishments, he frightened them with the punishments of the Hereafter, so he said: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire: ﴿that we have found what our Lord promised us to be true...﴾ to the end of the verses, and ﴿the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: Pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided you. They will say: Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers﴾. And when the people of the Fire call to Malik: ﴿Let your Lord put an end to us﴾, he will say: ﴿Indeed, you will remain﴾. And when they call to their Lord: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾, He will answer them: ﴿Remain in it, and do not speak to Me﴾. And when it is said to the polytheists: ﴿Call upon your partners,﴾ so they call upon them, ﴿but they will not respond to them﴾.

{33} So he frightened them, may Allah be pleased with him, with this awesome day, and he grieved for them if they persisted in their polytheism. For this reason he said: ﴿The day you turn back fleeing﴾, that is, you will have been driven to the Fire. ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾, neither from yourselves, having any strength by which you could repel the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone besides Him help you, ﴿the day the secrets are tested. Then he will have no power and no helper﴾. ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, because guidance is in the hand of Allah, the Exalted. When He withholds guidance from His servant, knowing that he is unworthy of it because of his corruption, there is no way to guide him.

{34} ﴿And Joseph certainly came to you﴾, son of Jacob, peace be upon them both, ﴿before﴾ the coming of Moses with the clear proofs that indicate his truthfulness, and he commanded you to worship your Lord alone with no partner. ﴿But you continued in doubt about what he brought you﴾ during his lifetime. ﴿Until when he died﴾, your doubt and polytheism increased, ﴿and you said: Allah will never send after him a messenger.﴾ That is: this is your false supposition and your presumption, which is not befitting of Allah, the Exalted. He, the Exalted, does not leave His creation neglected, not commanding them and forbidding them, but sends His messengers to them. To suppose that Allah does not send a messenger is a supposition of misguidance. For this reason He said: ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whoever is a transgressor [and doubter]﴾. This is their true description, by which they described Moses with injustice and arrogance. They are the transgressors, by exceeding the truth and deviating from it into error, and they are the liars, since they attributed that to Allah and denied His messenger. Whoever is characterized by transgression and lying, and does not depart from them, Allah does not guide, nor does He grant him success in good, because he rejected the truth after it reached him and he recognized it. So his recompense is that Allah punishes him by withholding guidance from him, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, ﴿and We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

{35} Then He mentioned the description of the transgressing liar, saying: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which have made the truth distinct from falsehood and have become, in their clarity, like the sun to sight. They dispute about them despite their clarity, in order to repel and nullify them, ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, that is, without any proof or evidence. This is a necessary description of everyone who disputes concerning the signs of Allah, for it is impossible to dispute with authority, because the truth is not opposed by any opponent. It is therefore impossible to oppose it with any legal or rational proof at all. ﴿Greatly hateful is that﴾ statement which includes rejecting the truth with falsehood, ﴿in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾. Allah is most intensely hostile to its speaker, because it contains denial of the truth, affirmation of falsehood, and attributing that to Him. These are matters that intensify Allah's hatred for them and for whoever is characterized by them. Likewise, His believing servants detest them with the utmost detestation, in agreement with their Lord. These are the elite of Allah's creation, so their detestation is evidence of the vileness of those they detest. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, as He sealed the hearts of the family of Pharaoh, ﴿Allah seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾, arrogant against the truth by rejecting it, and against people by belittling them, a tyrant through his excessive injustice and aggression.

{36–37} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing Moses and denying him in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is established upon the Throne and exalted above creation: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower﴾, that is, a great elevated structure, and its purpose is: ﴿that I may reach the heavens, and look at the God of Moses, though I think him to be a liar﴾ in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens. But he wanted to take precaution and test the matter himself. Allah, the Exalted, stated what moved him to this statement: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾. So the evil deed was made attractive to him, and Satan continued to adorn it for him, calling to it and making it seem good, until he saw it as good and called to it, and debated as one who is sincere would debate, though he was among the greatest corrupters. ﴿And he was barred from the way﴾, the truth, because of the falsehood that was made attractive to him. ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴾, that is, loss and destruction, which brought him nothing but misery in this world and the Hereafter. He intended by it to plot against the truth and to make people think that he was right and that Moses was in the wrong.

{38} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating his sincere advice to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, not as Pharaoh tells you, for he will guide you only to the way of error and corruption.

{39} ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is only a enjoyment﴾, enjoyed and delighted in for a little while, then it ends and vanishes. Do not let it deceive you and mislead you away from that for which you were created. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, the place of residence and the dwelling of rest and stability. So you ought to prefer it and work for it, with deeds that will make you happy there.

{40} ﴿Whoever does an evil deed﴾, whether polytheism, grave disobedience, or sin, ﴿will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, that is, he will be recompensed only with what will harm and grieve him, because the recompense for evil is evil. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, from deeds of the heart, the limbs, and the words of the tongue, ﴿those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account﴾, that is, they will be given their reward without limit or counting, rather Allah will give them what their deeds could never reach.

{41} ﴿And O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation﴾ through what I have told you, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾ by abandoning the following of the Prophet of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him.

{42} Then he explained that, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of﴾, that it deserves to be worshipped besides Allah, and speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most abominable sins. ﴿And I call you to the Mighty﴾, who possesses all power, while others have no part in the affair at all, ﴿the Forgiving﴾, who forgives His servants who are excessive against themselves and who dare to displease Him. When they repent and turn to Him, He removes their sins and wrongs and averts their causes of worldly and otherworldly punishments.

{43} ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, truly and certainly, ﴿that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is, it does not deserve to be called to nor to be sought for refuge in this world or the Hereafter, because of its weakness and deficiency, and because it possesses neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection. ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾, the Exalted, and He will recompense every doer according to his deeds. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, those who have transgressed against themselves by daring against their Lord with His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and no others.

{44} When he had advised them, warned them and admonished them, and they neither obeyed him nor agreed with him, he said to them: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ of this advice, and you will see the consequence of not accepting it when punishment befalls you and you are deprived of the great reward. ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾; that is, I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, cast all my affairs upon Him, and rely upon Him for my welfare and for averting the harm that may befall me from you or from others. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: He knows their conditions and what they deserve. He knows my condition and my weakness, so He will keep me safe from you and suffice me against your evil, and He knows your conditions, so you do not act except by His will and His decree; if He gives you power over me, then that proceeds from His wisdom, the Exalted, and from His will and decree.

{45–46} ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾; that is, Allah, the Strong, the Merciful, shielded that believing man, who was granted success, from the punishments of what Pharaoh and his household schemed against him, namely their intention to destroy and ruin him. This was because he confronted them with what they disliked, and openly showed complete agreement with Musa (peace be upon him), calling them to what Musa had called them to. This is something they could not tolerate, and they were the ones holding power at that time. He had angered them and their rage against him intensified, so they intended to harm him, but Allah protected him from their plot and scheme, and their plot and scheme turned back upon themselves. ﴿And there befell the household of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾: Allah drowned them all, to the last of them, in a single morning, and in the barzakh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour arises, [it will be said], "Admit the household of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ These are the dreadful punishments that befall those who deny the messengers of Allah and oppose His command.

{23} That is: ﴿And We indeed sent Moses﴾, son of Imran, to the kind of these deniers, ﴿with Our signs﴾, the great signs that decisively demonstrate the truth of what he was sent with and the falsehood of what those he was sent to held, namely polytheism and what follows from it, ﴿and a clear authority﴾. That is, a manifest proof that takes hold of hearts so that they submit to it, like the staff that became a serpent and similar clear signs with which Allah strengthened Moses and enabled him to establish the truth to which he called.

{24} The ones he was sent to were ﴿Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was of the people of Moses but who oppressed them with his wealth. All of them rejected him in the strongest manner and said: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾.

{25} ﴿When he came to them with the truth from Us﴾, supported by Allah with dazzling miracles that necessitate complete submission, they did not meet it with that. Mere abandonment and aversion did not suffice them, nor even denying it and opposing it with their falsehood. Rather, their vile condition reached the point that ﴿they said: Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women. But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾. They devised this scheme, supposing that if they killed their sons, the people would not grow strong and would remain in their servitude and under their bondage. Yet their plot was ﴿only in error﴾, for what they intended did not come to pass; rather, the opposite of what they intended befell them. Allah destroyed them and annihilated them to the last one.

For this reason He did not say, "Their plot is only in error," but said: ﴿And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.

{26} ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, arrogant, tyrannical, deceiving his foolish people: ﴿Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord﴾. That is, he claimed, may Allah disfigure him, that were it not for considering the feelings of his people, he would have killed him, and that the supplication of his Lord would not prevent him. Then he mentioned what moved him to intend killing him, claiming that it was sincere advice to his people and the removal of evil from the land, so he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾, which you follow, ﴿or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾. How most astonishing this is! That the most evil of creatures should advise people against following the best of creatures. This is from the deception and propaganda that enters only the minds of those about whom Allah said: ﴿So he made his people light-headed, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people﴾.

{27} ﴿And Moses said﴾, when Pharaoh uttered that vile statement that his tyranny had compelled him to make, relying on his power and authority, while seeking refuge in his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord﴾. That is, I have taken refuge in His lordship by which He governs all affairs ﴿from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account﴾. That is, his arrogance and his failure to believe in the Day of Account carry him to evil and corruption. Pharaoh and others are included in this, as was mentioned previously in the principle. So Allah, the Exalted, protected him by His kindness from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account, and provided for him the means by which the evil of Pharaoh and his chiefs was averted from him.

{28} Among the means was this believing man from the family of Pharaoh, from the house of the kingdom. He must have had an audible word, especially since he was showing agreement with them while concealing his faith. For they usually show him consideration in a way they would not if he opposed them openly. Likewise Allah protected His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) through his uncle Abu Talib from the Quraysh, since Abu Talib was a leader among them who agreed with them in their religion. Had he been a Muslim, that protection would not have come from him. So this believing man, the one granted success, intelligent and resolute, said, denouncing the deed of his people and the monstrousness of what they had resolved: ﴿Will you kill a man merely because he says: My Lord is Allah?﴾ That is: how can you consider it lawful to kill him when his sin and crime is that he says, "My Lord is Allah"? And it was not merely a statement devoid of proofs, which is why he said: ﴿And he has certainly come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾, because his clear evidence was well known among them, so that both the young and the old knew of it. That is: this does not necessitate his killing. So why did you not first refute what he brought of the truth and confront the proof with a proof that refutes it, and then consider whether it is lawful to kill him if you prevail over him with argument or not? As for now, when his argument has become evident and his proof has prevailed, then between you and the permissibility of killing him are deserts across which the necks of camels are broken.

Then he said to them a rational statement that satisfies every intelligent person in any circumstance: ﴿And if he is a liar, his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾. That is, Moses is between two situations: either he is a liar in his claim, or he is truthful in it. If he is a liar, then his lie is upon him and its harm is limited to him, and there is no harm to you in that, since you have refrained from answering and confirming him. If he is truthful, and he has come to you with clear proofs and informed you that if you do not respond to him, Allah will punish you with a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter, then some of what he promises you will certainly befall you, namely the punishment of this world. This is from his good intellect and gentle manner in defending Moses, since he presented this answer which leaves them no confusion, and made the matter revolve around these two states. In every case, killing him is folly and ignorance on your part.

Then he moved on, may Allah be pleased with him, grant him satisfaction, forgive him and have mercy on him, to a matter higher than that and to explaining Moses' closeness to the truth, so he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor﴾, that is, one who exceeds the limit by abandoning the truth and turning to falsehood, ﴿a liar﴾, by attributing to Allah what he has transgressed in. So Allah does not guide such a person to the path of right; neither in what he indicates nor in his proof, and he is not granted success on the straight path. That is: you have seen what Moses called to of the truth and what Allah guided him to explain of the rational proofs and heavenly marvels. Whoever is guided with such guidance cannot be a transgressor or a liar. This is evidence of his perfect knowledge, intellect and recognition of his Lord.

{29} Then he warned his people, advised them, and frightened them with the punishment of the Hereafter, and forbade them from being deceived by apparent sovereignty, so he said: ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿dominant in the land﴾ over your subjects, executing whatever arrangements you wish. ﴿So who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes to us?﴾ That is, His punishment. This is from the goodness of his call, since he made the matter shared between himself and them by saying ﴿who will help us﴾ and ﴿if it comes to us﴾, so as to make them understand that he gives sincere advice to them as he gives it to himself, and wishes for them what he wishes for himself. ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, opposing him in that and deceiving his people so that they would follow Moses: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. He spoke truly in saying ﴿I show you only what I see﴾, but what did he see? He saw that he should make his people light-headed so they would follow him, in order to secure his leadership over them. He did not see the truth with him; rather he saw the truth with Moses and denied it while being certain of it. He lied in saying ﴿I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾, for this is an inversion of the truth. Had he commanded them to follow him merely in his disbelief and error, the evil would have been lighter. But he commanded them to follow him, claiming that in following him is following the truth, and in following the truth is following error.

{30} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating the call to his people, not despairing of their guidance, as is the state of those who call to Allah, the Exalted. They do not cease calling to their Lord, nor is anyone who turns them away able to stop them from repeating the call, nor does the obstinacy of those they call deter them. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾, meaning the deniers among past nations who banded together against their prophets and united to oppose them.

{31} Then he explained them, saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud and those after them﴾, that is, like their habit of disbelief and denial, and Allah's custom with them of swift punishment in this world before the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice to the servants﴾, so that He would punish them without a sin they committed or a crime they had earlier perpetrated.

{32} When he had frightened them with worldly punishments, he frightened them with the punishments of the Hereafter, so he said: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire: ﴿that we have found what our Lord promised us to be true...﴾ to the end of the verses, and ﴿the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: Pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided you. They will say: Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers﴾. And when the people of the Fire call to Malik: ﴿Let your Lord put an end to us﴾, he will say: ﴿Indeed, you will remain﴾. And when they call to their Lord: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾, He will answer them: ﴿Remain in it, and do not speak to Me﴾. And when it is said to the polytheists: ﴿Call upon your partners,﴾ so they call upon them, ﴿but they will not respond to them﴾.

{33} So he frightened them, may Allah be pleased with him, with this awesome day, and he grieved for them if they persisted in their polytheism. For this reason he said: ﴿The day you turn back fleeing﴾, that is, you will have been driven to the Fire. ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾, neither from yourselves, having any strength by which you could repel the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone besides Him help you, ﴿the day the secrets are tested. Then he will have no power and no helper﴾. ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, because guidance is in the hand of Allah, the Exalted. When He withholds guidance from His servant, knowing that he is unworthy of it because of his corruption, there is no way to guide him.

{34} ﴿And Joseph certainly came to you﴾, son of Jacob, peace be upon them both, ﴿before﴾ the coming of Moses with the clear proofs that indicate his truthfulness, and he commanded you to worship your Lord alone with no partner. ﴿But you continued in doubt about what he brought you﴾ during his lifetime. ﴿Until when he died﴾, your doubt and polytheism increased, ﴿and you said: Allah will never send after him a messenger.﴾ That is: this is your false supposition and your presumption, which is not befitting of Allah, the Exalted. He, the Exalted, does not leave His creation neglected, not commanding them and forbidding them, but sends His messengers to them. To suppose that Allah does not send a messenger is a supposition of misguidance. For this reason He said: ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whoever is a transgressor [and doubter]﴾. This is their true description, by which they described Moses with injustice and arrogance. They are the transgressors, by exceeding the truth and deviating from it into error, and they are the liars, since they attributed that to Allah and denied His messenger. Whoever is characterized by transgression and lying, and does not depart from them, Allah does not guide, nor does He grant him success in good, because he rejected the truth after it reached him and he recognized it. So his recompense is that Allah punishes him by withholding guidance from him, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, ﴿and We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

{35} Then He mentioned the description of the transgressing liar, saying: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which have made the truth distinct from falsehood and have become, in their clarity, like the sun to sight. They dispute about them despite their clarity, in order to repel and nullify them, ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, that is, without any proof or evidence. This is a necessary description of everyone who disputes concerning the signs of Allah, for it is impossible to dispute with authority, because the truth is not opposed by any opponent. It is therefore impossible to oppose it with any legal or rational proof at all. ﴿Greatly hateful is that﴾ statement which includes rejecting the truth with falsehood, ﴿in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾. Allah is most intensely hostile to its speaker, because it contains denial of the truth, affirmation of falsehood, and attributing that to Him. These are matters that intensify Allah's hatred for them and for whoever is characterized by them. Likewise, His believing servants detest them with the utmost detestation, in agreement with their Lord. These are the elite of Allah's creation, so their detestation is evidence of the vileness of those they detest. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, as He sealed the hearts of the family of Pharaoh, ﴿Allah seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾, arrogant against the truth by rejecting it, and against people by belittling them, a tyrant through his excessive injustice and aggression.

{36–37} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing Moses and denying him in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is established upon the Throne and exalted above creation: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower﴾, that is, a great elevated structure, and its purpose is: ﴿that I may reach the heavens, and look at the God of Moses, though I think him to be a liar﴾ in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens. But he wanted to take precaution and test the matter himself. Allah, the Exalted, stated what moved him to this statement: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾. So the evil deed was made attractive to him, and Satan continued to adorn it for him, calling to it and making it seem good, until he saw it as good and called to it, and debated as one who is sincere would debate, though he was among the greatest corrupters. ﴿And he was barred from the way﴾, the truth, because of the falsehood that was made attractive to him. ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴾, that is, loss and destruction, which brought him nothing but misery in this world and the Hereafter. He intended by it to plot against the truth and to make people think that he was right and that Moses was in the wrong.

{38} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating his sincere advice to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, not as Pharaoh tells you, for he will guide you only to the way of error and corruption.

{39} ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is only a enjoyment﴾, enjoyed and delighted in for a little while, then it ends and vanishes. Do not let it deceive you and mislead you away from that for which you were created. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, the place of residence and the dwelling of rest and stability. So you ought to prefer it and work for it, with deeds that will make you happy there.

{40} ﴿Whoever does an evil deed﴾, whether polytheism, grave disobedience, or sin, ﴿will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, that is, he will be recompensed only with what will harm and grieve him, because the recompense for evil is evil. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, from deeds of the heart, the limbs, and the words of the tongue, ﴿those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account﴾, that is, they will be given their reward without limit or counting, rather Allah will give them what their deeds could never reach.

{41} ﴿And O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation﴾ through what I have told you, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾ by abandoning the following of the Prophet of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him.

{42} Then he explained that, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of﴾, that it deserves to be worshipped besides Allah, and speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most abominable sins. ﴿And I call you to the Mighty﴾, who possesses all power, while others have no part in the affair at all, ﴿the Forgiving﴾, who forgives His servants who are excessive against themselves and who dare to displease Him. When they repent and turn to Him, He removes their sins and wrongs and averts their causes of worldly and otherworldly punishments.

{43} ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, truly and certainly, ﴿that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is, it does not deserve to be called to nor to be sought for refuge in this world or the Hereafter, because of its weakness and deficiency, and because it possesses neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection. ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾, the Exalted, and He will recompense every doer according to his deeds. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, those who have transgressed against themselves by daring against their Lord with His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and no others.

{44} When he had advised them, warned them and admonished them, and they neither obeyed him nor agreed with him, he said to them: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ of this advice, and you will see the consequence of not accepting it when punishment befalls you and you are deprived of the great reward. ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾; that is, I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, cast all my affairs upon Him, and rely upon Him for my welfare and for averting the harm that may befall me from you or from others. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: He knows their conditions and what they deserve. He knows my condition and my weakness, so He will keep me safe from you and suffice me against your evil, and He knows your conditions, so you do not act except by His will and His decree; if He gives you power over me, then that proceeds from His wisdom, the Exalted, and from His will and decree.

{45–46} ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾; that is, Allah, the Strong, the Merciful, shielded that believing man, who was granted success, from the punishments of what Pharaoh and his household schemed against him, namely their intention to destroy and ruin him. This was because he confronted them with what they disliked, and openly showed complete agreement with Musa (peace be upon him), calling them to what Musa had called them to. This is something they could not tolerate, and they were the ones holding power at that time. He had angered them and their rage against him intensified, so they intended to harm him, but Allah protected him from their plot and scheme, and their plot and scheme turned back upon themselves. ﴿And there befell the household of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾: Allah drowned them all, to the last of them, in a single morning, and in the barzakh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour arises, [it will be said], "Admit the household of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ These are the dreadful punishments that befall those who deny the messengers of Allah and oppose His command.

{23} That is: ﴿And We indeed sent Moses﴾, son of Imran, to the kind of these deniers, ﴿with Our signs﴾, the great signs that decisively demonstrate the truth of what he was sent with and the falsehood of what those he was sent to held, namely polytheism and what follows from it, ﴿and a clear authority﴾. That is, a manifest proof that takes hold of hearts so that they submit to it, like the staff that became a serpent and similar clear signs with which Allah strengthened Moses and enabled him to establish the truth to which he called.

{24} The ones he was sent to were ﴿Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was of the people of Moses but who oppressed them with his wealth. All of them rejected him in the strongest manner and said: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾.

{25} ﴿When he came to them with the truth from Us﴾, supported by Allah with dazzling miracles that necessitate complete submission, they did not meet it with that. Mere abandonment and aversion did not suffice them, nor even denying it and opposing it with their falsehood. Rather, their vile condition reached the point that ﴿they said: Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women. But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾. They devised this scheme, supposing that if they killed their sons, the people would not grow strong and would remain in their servitude and under their bondage. Yet their plot was ﴿only in error﴾, for what they intended did not come to pass; rather, the opposite of what they intended befell them. Allah destroyed them and annihilated them to the last one.

Principle: Reflect on this point, which frequently recurs in the Book of Allah, the Exalted: when the context concerns a particular story or a particular matter, and Allah wishes to pass a ruling on that particular matter that is not restricted to it, He states the ruling and attaches it to a general description, so that it is more comprehensive, includes the case for which the discourse was brought, and removes the misconception that the ruling is restricted to that particular matter. For this reason He did not say, "Their plot is only in error," but said: ﴿And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.
