They are the transgressors, by exceeding the truth and deviating from it into error, and they are the liars, since they attributed that to Allah and denied His messenger. Whoever is characterized by transgression and lying, and does not depart from them, Allah does not guide, nor does He grant him success in good, because he rejected the truth after it reached him and he recognized it. So his recompense is that Allah punishes him by withholding guidance from him, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, ﴿and We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

{35} Then He mentioned the description of the transgressing liar, saying: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which have made the truth distinct from falsehood and have become, in their clarity, like the sun to sight. They dispute about them despite their clarity, in order to repel and nullify them, ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, that is, without any proof or evidence. This is a necessary description of everyone who disputes concerning the signs of Allah, for it is impossible to dispute with authority, because the truth is not opposed by any opponent. It is therefore impossible to oppose it with any legal or rational proof at all. ﴿Greatly hateful is that﴾ statement which includes rejecting the truth with falsehood, ﴿in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾. Allah is most intensely hostile to its speaker, because it contains denial of the truth, affirmation of falsehood, and attributing that to Him. These are matters that intensify Allah's hatred for them and for whoever is characterized by them. Likewise, His believing servants detest them with the utmost detestation, in agreement with their Lord. These are the elite of Allah's creation, so their detestation is evidence of the vileness of those they detest. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, as He sealed the hearts of the family of Pharaoh, ﴿Allah seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾, arrogant against the truth by rejecting it, and against people by belittling them, a tyrant through his excessive injustice and aggression.

{36–37} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing Moses and denying him in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is established upon the Throne and exalted above creation: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower﴾, that is, a great elevated structure, and its purpose is: ﴿that I may reach the heavens, and look at the God of Moses, though I think him to be a liar﴾ in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens. But he wanted to take precaution and test the matter himself. Allah, the Exalted, stated what moved him to this statement: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾. So the evil deed was made attractive to him, and Satan continued to adorn it for him, calling to it and making it seem good, until he saw it as good and called to it, and debated as one who is sincere would debate, though he was among the greatest corrupters. ﴿And he was barred from the way﴾, the truth, because of the falsehood that was made attractive to him. ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴾, that is, loss and destruction, which brought him nothing but misery in this world and the Hereafter. He intended by it to plot against the truth and to make people think that he was right and that Moses was in the wrong.

{38} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating his sincere advice to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, not as Pharaoh tells you, for he will guide you only to the way of error and corruption.

{39} ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is only a enjoyment﴾, enjoyed and delighted in for a little while, then it ends and vanishes. Do not let it deceive you and mislead you away from that for which you were created. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, the place of residence and the dwelling of rest and stability. So you ought to prefer it and work for it, with deeds that will make you happy there.

{40} ﴿Whoever does an evil deed﴾, whether polytheism, grave disobedience, or sin, ﴿will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, that is, he will be recompensed only with what will harm and grieve him, because the recompense for evil is evil. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, from deeds of the heart, the limbs, and the words of the tongue, ﴿those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account﴾, that is, they will be given their reward without limit or counting, rather Allah will give them what their deeds could never reach.

{41} ﴿And O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation﴾ through what I have told you, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾ by abandoning the following of the Prophet of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him.

{42} Then he explained that, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of﴾, that it deserves to be worshipped besides Allah, and speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most abominable sins. ﴿And I call you to the Mighty﴾, who possesses all power, while others have no part in the affair at all, ﴿the Forgiving﴾, who forgives His servants who are excessive against themselves and who dare to displease Him. When they repent and turn to Him, He removes their sins and wrongs and averts their causes of worldly and otherworldly punishments.

{43} ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, truly and certainly, ﴿that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is, it does not deserve to be called to nor to be sought for refuge in this world or the Hereafter, because of its weakness and deficiency, and because it possesses neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection. ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾, the Exalted, and He will recompense every doer according to his deeds. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, those who have transgressed against themselves by daring against their Lord with His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and no others.

{44} When he had advised them, warned them and admonished them, and they neither obeyed him nor agreed with him, he said to them: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ of this advice, and you will see the consequence of not accepting it when punishment befalls you and you are deprived of the great reward. ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾; that is, I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, cast all my affairs upon Him, and rely upon Him for my welfare and for averting the harm that may befall me from you or from others. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: He knows their conditions and what they deserve. He knows my condition and my weakness, so He will keep me safe from you and suffice me against your evil, and He knows your conditions, so you do not act except by His will and His decree; if He gives you power over me, then that proceeds from His wisdom, the Exalted, and from His will and decree.

{45–46} ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾; that is, Allah, the Strong, the Merciful, shielded that believing man, who was granted success, from the punishments of what Pharaoh and his household schemed against him, namely their intention to destroy and ruin him. This was because he confronted them with what they disliked, and openly showed complete agreement with Musa (peace be upon him), calling them to what Musa had called them to. This is something they could not tolerate, and they were the ones holding power at that time. He had angered them and their rage against him intensified, so they intended to harm him, but Allah protected him from their plot and scheme, and their plot and scheme turned back upon themselves. ﴿And there befell the household of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾: Allah drowned them all, to the last of them, in a single morning, and in the barzakh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour arises, [it will be said], "Admit the household of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ These are the dreadful punishments that befall those who deny the messengers of Allah and oppose His command.

{23} That is: ﴿And We indeed sent Moses﴾, son of Imran, to the kind of these deniers, ﴿with Our signs﴾, the great signs that decisively demonstrate the truth of what he was sent with and the falsehood of what those he was sent to held, namely polytheism and what follows from it, ﴿and a clear authority﴾. That is, a manifest proof that takes hold of hearts so that they submit to it, like the staff that became a serpent and similar clear signs with which Allah strengthened Moses and enabled him to establish the truth to which he called.

{24} The ones he was sent to were ﴿Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was of the people of Moses but who oppressed them with his wealth. All of them rejected him in the strongest manner and said: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾.

{25} ﴿When he came to them with the truth from Us﴾, supported by Allah with dazzling miracles that necessitate complete submission, they did not meet it with that. Mere abandonment and aversion did not suffice them, nor even denying it and opposing it with their falsehood. Rather, their vile condition reached the point that ﴿they said: Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women. But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾. They devised this scheme, supposing that if they killed their sons, the people would not grow strong and would remain in their servitude and under their bondage. Yet their plot was ﴿only in error﴾, for what they intended did not come to pass; rather, the opposite of what they intended befell them. Allah destroyed them and annihilated them to the last one.

Principle: Reflect on this point, which frequently recurs in the Book of Allah, the Exalted: when the context concerns a particular story or a particular matter, and Allah wishes to pass a ruling on that particular matter that is not restricted to it, He states the ruling and attaches it to a general description, so that it is more comprehensive, includes the case for which the discourse was brought, and removes the misconception that the ruling is restricted to that particular matter. For this reason He did not say, "Their plot is only in error," but said: ﴿And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error﴾.

{26} ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, arrogant, tyrannical, deceiving his foolish people: ﴿Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord﴾. That is, he claimed, may Allah disfigure him, that were it not for considering the feelings of his people, he would have killed him, and that the supplication of his Lord would not prevent him. Then he mentioned what moved him to intend killing him, claiming that it was sincere advice to his people and the removal of evil from the land, so he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾, which you follow, ﴿or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾. How most astonishing this is! That the most evil of creatures should advise people against following the best of creatures. This is from the deception and propaganda that enters only the minds of those about whom Allah said: ﴿So he made his people light-headed, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people﴾.

{27} ﴿And Moses said﴾, when Pharaoh uttered that vile statement that his tyranny had compelled him to make, relying on his power and authority, while seeking refuge in his Lord: ﴿Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord﴾. That is, I have taken refuge in His lordship by which He governs all affairs ﴿from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account﴾. That is, his arrogance and his failure to believe in the Day of Account carry him to evil and corruption. Pharaoh and others are included in this, as was mentioned previously in the principle. So Allah, the Exalted, protected him by His kindness from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account, and provided for him the means by which the evil of Pharaoh and his chiefs was averted from him.

{28} Among the means was this believing man from the family of Pharaoh, from the house of the kingdom. He must have had an audible word, especially since he was showing agreement with them while concealing his faith. For they usually show him consideration in a way they would not if he opposed them openly. Likewise Allah protected His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) through his uncle Abu Talib from the Quraysh, since Abu Talib was a leader among them who agreed with them in their religion. Had he been a Muslim, that protection would not have come from him. So this believing man, the one granted success, intelligent and resolute, said, denouncing the deed of his people and the monstrousness of what they had resolved: ﴿Will you kill a man merely because he says: My Lord is Allah?﴾ That is: how can you consider it lawful to kill him when his sin and crime is that he says, "My Lord is Allah"? And it was not merely a statement devoid of proofs, which is why he said: ﴿And he has certainly come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾, because his clear evidence was well known among them, so that both the young and the old knew of it. That is: this does not necessitate his killing. So why did you not first refute what he brought of the truth and confront the proof with a proof that refutes it, and then consider whether it is lawful to kill him if you prevail over him with argument or not? As for now, when his argument has become evident and his proof has prevailed, then between you and the permissibility of killing him are deserts across which the necks of camels are broken.

Then he said to them a rational statement that satisfies every intelligent person in any circumstance: ﴿And if he is a liar, his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾. That is, Moses is between two situations: either he is a liar in his claim, or he is truthful in it. If he is a liar, then his lie is upon him and its harm is limited to him, and there is no harm to you in that, since you have refrained from answering and confirming him. If he is truthful, and he has come to you with clear proofs and informed you that if you do not respond to him, Allah will punish you with a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter, then some of what he promises you will certainly befall you, namely the punishment of this world. This is from his good intellect and gentle manner in defending Moses, since he presented this answer which leaves them no confusion, and made the matter revolve around these two states. In every case, killing him is folly and ignorance on your part.

Then he moved on, may Allah be pleased with him, grant him satisfaction, forgive him and have mercy on him, to a matter higher than that and to explaining Moses' closeness to the truth, so he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor﴾, that is, one who exceeds the limit by abandoning the truth and turning to falsehood, ﴿a liar﴾, by attributing to Allah what he has transgressed in. So Allah does not guide such a person to the path of right; neither in what he indicates nor in his proof, and he is not granted success on the straight path. That is: you have seen what Moses called to of the truth and what Allah guided him to explain of the rational proofs and heavenly marvels. Whoever is guided with such guidance cannot be a transgressor or a liar. This is evidence of his perfect knowledge, intellect and recognition of his Lord.

{29} Then he warned his people, advised them, and frightened them with the punishment of the Hereafter, and forbade them from being deceived by apparent sovereignty, so he said: ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿dominant in the land﴾ over your subjects, executing whatever arrangements you wish. ﴿So who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes to us?﴾ That is, His punishment. This is from the goodness of his call, since he made the matter shared between himself and them by saying ﴿who will help us﴾ and ﴿if it comes to us﴾, so as to make them understand that he gives sincere advice to them as he gives it to himself, and wishes for them what he wishes for himself. ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, opposing him in that and deceiving his people so that they would follow Moses: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. He spoke truly in saying ﴿I show you only what I see﴾, but what did he see? He saw that he should make his people light-headed so they would follow him, in order to secure his leadership over them. He did not see the truth with him; rather he saw the truth with Moses and denied it while being certain of it. He lied in saying ﴿I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾, for this is an inversion of the truth. Had he commanded them to follow him merely in his disbelief and error, the evil would have been lighter. But he commanded them to follow him, claiming that in following him is following the truth, and in following the truth is following error.

{30} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating the call to his people, not despairing of their guidance, as is the state of those who call to Allah, the Exalted. They do not cease calling to their Lord, nor is anyone who turns them away able to stop them from repeating the call, nor does the obstinacy of those they call deter them. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾, meaning the deniers among past nations who banded together against their prophets and united to oppose them.

{31} Then he explained them, saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud and those after them﴾, that is, like their habit of disbelief and denial, and Allah's custom with them of swift punishment in this world before the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice to the servants﴾, so that He would punish them without a sin they committed or a crime they had earlier perpetrated.

{32} When he had frightened them with worldly punishments, he frightened them with the punishments of the Hereafter, so he said: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire: ﴿that we have found what our Lord promised us to be true...﴾ to the end of the verses, and ﴿the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: Pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided you. They will say: Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers﴾. And when the people of the Fire call to Malik: ﴿Let your Lord put an end to us﴾, he will say: ﴿Indeed, you will remain﴾. And when they call to their Lord: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾, He will answer them: ﴿Remain in it, and do not speak to Me﴾. And when it is said to the polytheists: ﴿Call upon your partners,﴾ so they call upon them, ﴿but they will not respond to them﴾.

{33} So he frightened them, may Allah be pleased with him, with this awesome day, and he grieved for them if they persisted in their polytheism. For this reason he said: ﴿The day you turn back fleeing﴾, that is, you will have been driven to the Fire. ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾, neither from yourselves, having any strength by which you could repel the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone besides Him help you, ﴿the day the secrets are tested. Then he will have no power and no helper﴾. ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, because guidance is in the hand of Allah, the Exalted. When He withholds guidance from His servant, knowing that he is unworthy of it because of his corruption, there is no way to guide him.

{34} ﴿And Joseph certainly came to you﴾, son of Jacob, peace be upon them both, ﴿before﴾ the coming of Moses with the clear proofs that indicate his truthfulness, and he commanded you to worship your Lord alone with no partner. ﴿But you continued in doubt about what he brought you﴾ during his lifetime. ﴿Until when he died﴾, your doubt and polytheism increased, ﴿and you said: Allah will never send after him a messenger.﴾ That is: this is your false supposition and your presumption, which is not befitting of Allah, the Exalted. He, the Exalted, does not leave His creation neglected, not commanding them and forbidding them, but sends His messengers to them. To suppose that Allah does not send a messenger is a supposition of misguidance. For this reason He said: ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whoever is a transgressor [and doubter]﴾. This is their true description, by which they described Moses with injustice and arrogance. They are the transgressors, by exceeding the truth and deviating from it into error, and they are the liars, since they attributed that to Allah and denied His messenger. Whoever is characterized by transgression and lying, and does not depart from them, Allah does not guide, nor does He grant him success in good, because he rejected the truth after it reached him and he recognized it. So his recompense is that Allah punishes him by withholding guidance from him, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, ﴿and We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

{35} Then He mentioned the description of the transgressing liar, saying: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which have made the truth distinct from falsehood and have become, in their clarity, like the sun to sight. They dispute about them despite their clarity, in order to repel and nullify them, ﴿without authority having come to them﴾, that is, without any proof or evidence. This is a necessary description of everyone who disputes concerning the signs of Allah, for it is impossible to dispute with authority, because the truth is not opposed by any opponent. It is therefore impossible to oppose it with any legal or rational proof at all. ﴿Greatly hateful is that﴾ statement which includes rejecting the truth with falsehood, ﴿in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾. Allah is most intensely hostile to its speaker, because it contains denial of the truth, affirmation of falsehood, and attributing that to Him. These are matters that intensify Allah's hatred for them and for whoever is characterized by them. Likewise, His believing servants detest them with the utmost detestation, in agreement with their Lord. These are the elite of Allah's creation, so their detestation is evidence of the vileness of those they detest. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, as He sealed the hearts of the family of Pharaoh, ﴿Allah seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾, arrogant against the truth by rejecting it, and against people by belittling them, a tyrant through his excessive injustice and aggression.

{36–37} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing Moses and denying him in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds, who is established upon the Throne and exalted above creation: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower﴾, that is, a great elevated structure, and its purpose is: ﴿that I may reach the heavens, and look at the God of Moses, though I think him to be a liar﴾ in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens. But he wanted to take precaution and test the matter himself. Allah, the Exalted, stated what moved him to this statement: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾. So the evil deed was made attractive to him, and Satan continued to adorn it for him, calling to it and making it seem good, until he saw it as good and called to it, and debated as one who is sincere would debate, though he was among the greatest corrupters. ﴿And he was barred from the way﴾, the truth, because of the falsehood that was made attractive to him. ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴾, that is, loss and destruction, which brought him nothing but misery in this world and the Hereafter. He intended by it to plot against the truth and to make people think that he was right and that Moses was in the wrong.

{38} ﴿And the one who believed said﴾, repeating his sincere advice to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾, not as Pharaoh tells you, for he will guide you only to the way of error and corruption.

{39} ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is only a enjoyment﴾, enjoyed and delighted in for a little while, then it ends and vanishes. Do not let it deceive you and mislead you away from that for which you were created. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, the place of residence and the dwelling of rest and stability. So you ought to prefer it and work for it, with deeds that will make you happy there.

{40} ﴿Whoever does an evil deed﴾, whether polytheism, grave disobedience, or sin, ﴿will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, that is, he will be recompensed only with what will harm and grieve him, because the recompense for evil is evil. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female﴾, from deeds of the heart, the limbs, and the words of the tongue, ﴿those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account﴾, that is, they will be given their reward without limit or counting, rather Allah will give them what their deeds could never reach.

{41} ﴿And O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation﴾ through what I have told you, ﴿while you call me to the Fire﴾ by abandoning the following of the Prophet of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him.

{42} Then he explained that, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of﴾, that it deserves to be worshipped besides Allah, and speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most abominable sins. ﴿And I call you to the Mighty﴾, who possesses all power, while others have no part in the affair at all, ﴿the Forgiving﴾, who forgives His servants who are excessive against themselves and who dare to displease Him. When they repent and turn to Him, He removes their sins and wrongs and averts their causes of worldly and otherworldly punishments.

{43} ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, truly and certainly, ﴿that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is, it does not deserve to be called to nor to be sought for refuge in this world or the Hereafter, because of its weakness and deficiency, and because it possesses neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection. ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾, the Exalted, and He will recompense every doer according to his deeds. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, those who have transgressed against themselves by daring against their Lord with His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and no others.

{44} When he had advised them, warned them and admonished them, and they neither obeyed him nor agreed with him, he said to them: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾ of this advice, and you will see the consequence of not accepting it when punishment befalls you and you are deprived of the great reward. ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾; that is, I take refuge in Him, seek His protection, cast all my affairs upon Him, and rely upon Him for my welfare and for averting the harm that may befall me from you or from others. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: He knows their conditions and what they deserve. He knows my condition and my weakness, so He will keep me safe from you and suffice me against your evil, and He knows your conditions, so you do not act except by His will and His decree; if He gives you power over me, then that proceeds from His wisdom, the Exalted, and from His will and decree.

{45–46} ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾; that is, Allah, the Strong, the Merciful, shielded that believing man, who was granted success, from the punishments of what Pharaoh and his household schemed against him, namely their intention to destroy and ruin him. This was because he confronted them with what they disliked, and openly showed complete agreement with Musa (peace be upon him), calling them to what Musa had called them to. This is something they could not tolerate, and they were the ones holding power at that time. He had angered them and their rage against him intensified, so they intended to harm him, but Allah protected him from their plot and scheme, and their plot and scheme turned back upon themselves. ﴿And there befell the household of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾: Allah drowned them all, to the last of them, in a single morning, and in the barzakh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour arises, [it will be said], "Admit the household of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ These are the dreadful punishments that befall those who deny the messengers of Allah and oppose His command.

{47} Almighty God informs us about the people of the Fire disputing with one another, blaming one another, seeking help from the guardians of the Fire, and the uselessness of doing so. He says: ﴿And when they argue within the Fire﴾: the followers argue by pointing to the misguidance of those they followed, and the leaders disown the followers. ﴿Then the weak will say﴾, that is, the followers to the leaders who were arrogant toward the truth and invited them to what they had been arrogant about: ﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾, meaning you misled us and led us astray, and you made shirk and evil appealing to us, ﴿so will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?﴾, that is, even a little.

{48} ﴿Those who were arrogant will say﴾, explaining their own helplessness and the enforcement of God's judgment over all of them: ﴿Indeed, we are all within it. Indeed, God has judged between the servants﴾, and assigned to each his share of punishment. So nothing is added to it, nothing is subtracted from it, and what the All-Wise has decreed is not changed.

{49} ﴿And those in the Fire will say﴾, from among the arrogant and the weak, ﴿to the guardians of Hell: "Call upon your Lord that He may lighten for us a day of the punishment"﴾: perhaps some relief may be obtained.

{50} ﴿They will say﴾, rebuking them and making clear that their intercession will not benefit them and their supplication will not avail them anything: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?﴾, by which you were made to distinguish the truth, the straight path, what brings one near to God, and what distances one from Him. ﴿They will say, "Yes"﴾: indeed they came to us with clear proofs, and God's conclusive argument was established against us, so we wronged and obstinately opposed the truth after it had become clear. ﴿They will say﴾, that is, the guardians say to the people of the Fire, disavowing any supplication or intercession on their behalf: ﴿So call upon [Him]﴾, you yourselves, but will this supplication avail anything or not? God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is not except in error﴾, that is, it is false and futile, because disbelief nullifies all deeds and prevents the answering of supplication.

{47} Almighty God informs us about the people of the Fire disputing with one another, blaming one another, seeking help from the guardians of the Fire, and the uselessness of doing so. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 53–55:

{53–54} When He had mentioned what happened to Musa and Fir'awn, and the outcome of Fir'awn's affair and his soldiers, and then mentioned the general ruling that encompasses him and the people of the Fire, He mentioned that He gave Musa {the guidance}; that is, the signs and the knowledge by which those who seek guidance are guided. {And We made the Children of Israel inherit the Book}; that is, We made it a heritage passed among them from one generation to another. It is the Torah. That Book contains guidance, which is knowledge of the legal rulings and other matters, and a reminder of good through encouragement toward it and of evil through warning against it. This is not for everyone; it is only for {people of understanding}.

{55} {So be patient}: O Messenger, just as those before you among the steadfast Messengers of resolve were patient. {Indeed, the promise of Allah is true}; that is, it is not doubtful, nor is there any uncertainty or falsehood in it, such that patience would be difficult for you. Rather, it is pure truth and unmixed guidance, upon which the patient endure and in holding fast to which the people of insight strive. So His saying {Indeed, the promise of Allah is true} is among the means that urge patience in obedience to Allah and in refraining from what Allah dislikes. {And ask forgiveness for your sin}: that which prevents you from attaining your success and happiness. So He commanded him to be patient, which brings about what is loved, and to seek forgiveness, which repels what is feared, and to glorify the praise of Allah, the Exalted, especially {in the evening and the morning}: the two best times, containing the litanies, obligatory and recommended duties that they contain, because in that there is help in all matters.

Allah, exalted is He, informs that whoever disputes concerning His signs, seeking to nullify them with falsehood and without any evidence from Him or any proof, this comes from arrogance in their breasts toward the truth and toward the one who brought it. They intend to prevail over it by means of the falsehood they possess. This is their aim and their purpose, but it will not be accomplished for them, and they will not attain it. This is an explicit text and good news that everyone who disputes the truth will be defeated, and everyone who is arrogant toward it will end up humiliated.

﴿So seek refuge﴾; i.e., take shelter and resort ﴿to Allah﴾. He did not mention what one seeks refuge from, intending generality; i.e., seek refuge in Allah from the arrogance that necessitates haughtiness toward the truth, seek refuge in Allah from the devils of mankind and the jinn, and seek refuge in Allah from all evils. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾: of all voices in their variety. ﴿the All-Seeing﴾: of all things seen, in whatever place, position, and time they may be.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 57–59:

{57} He, may He be exalted, informs of what is established in the intellects: that the creation of the heavens and the earth, despite their immensity and vastness, is greater, ﴿and greater than the creation of mankind﴾. For mankind, in comparison to the creation of the heavens and the earth, is among the smallest of things. So He who created the great celestial bodies and perfected them is able, all the more so and more fittingly, to restore people after their death. This is one of the rational proofs that indicate the resurrection with a decisive indication, by the mere contemplation of an intelligent person upon it. By it one reasons to a conclusion that admits of no doubt or uncertainty: the occurrence of what the messengers reported concerning the resurrection. Not everyone directs his thought to this or accepts it upon reflection, and so He said: ﴿but most people do not know﴾, meaning that they therefore do not take heed from this, nor do they bring it to mind.

{58} Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer﴾. That is: just as the blind and the seeing are not equal, so too are not equal the one who believes in God and does righteous deeds and the one who is arrogant toward worshipping his Lord, persistent in his disobedience, and striving in what displeases Him. ﴿Little do you remember﴾, meaning your remembrance is little. Otherwise, if you had reflected upon the ranks of matters, the stations of good and evil, and the distinction between the righteous and the wicked, and if you had lofty aspirations, you would have preferred what benefits over what harms, guidance over misguidance, and lasting happiness over the perishing world.

{59} ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it﴾. The messengers, who are the most truthful of creation, have informed of it, the heavenly books that speak of it have all their reports at the highest level of truthfulness, and the visible evidences and the horizon signs bear witness to it. ﴿But most people do not believe﴾ despite these matters that necessitate complete affirmation and submission.

{60} This is from His kindness to His servants and His great blessing: He called them to that which is good for their religion and their worldly life, commanded them to call upon Him, both the call of worship and the call of request, and promised that He would respond to them. And He threatened those who are arrogant toward it, so He said: {Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled} (dakhirin); that is, abased and despised, with punishment and humiliation gathered upon them as recompense for their arrogance.

Reflect upon these noble verses, which indicate the vastness of Allah's mercy, the abundance of His bounty, the obligation of thanking Him, the perfection of His power, the greatness of His authority, the breadth of His dominion, the comprehensiveness of His creation of all things, the perfection of His life, and His being worthy of praise for every perfect attribute with which He is characterized and every good act He has done, and the completeness of His lordship and His sole possession of it. They also indicate that all management in the higher and lower worlds, in past, present and future times, is in the hand of Allah the Exalted; no one has any share of the command or any share of power. From this it follows that He, the Exalted, is the one deity worthy of worship alone, Who deserves none of worship just as He deserves none of lordship. From this also follows the filling of hearts with knowledge of Allah the Exalted, with love of Him, fear of Him and hope in Him. These two matters, namely knowing Him and worshipping Him, are the very purpose for which Allah created creation; they are the ultimate aim intended by the Exalted for His servants; they are what lead to every good, success, righteousness and happiness in this world and the next; and they are [the two that are] the most noble gifts of the Generous to His servants, and the most noble pleasures absolutely. If these two are lost, every good is lost and every evil is present. So we ask the Exalted to fill our hearts with knowledge of Him and love for Him, and to make our inward and outward movements sincere for His sake, following His command; indeed He is not burdened by any request, nor is He diminished by any gift.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 61–65:

{61} As for the words of the Most High: ﴿Allah is the One who made the night for you﴾; that is, for your sake Allah made the night dark, ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ from your movements which, if they continued, would cause harm; so you retire to your bedding, and Allah casts upon you sleep, by which the heart and the body find rest. It is one of the essential needs of the human being; he cannot live without it. Also, every beloved finds tranquility with his beloved therein, thought gathers, and preoccupations decrease. ﴿And﴾ the Most High made ﴿the day to give sight﴾: bright with the sun that moves continuously in its orbit. So you rise from your beds to your worldly and religious occupations: this one for his remembrance and recitation (of Allah), this one for his prayer, this one for seeking knowledge and studying it, this one for his buying and selling, this one for his building, or his smithing, or similar crafts, this one for his travel by land and sea, this one for his farming, and this one for tending his animals. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty﴾; that is, great, as the indefiniteness indicates, ﴿toward mankind﴾, in that He has bestowed upon them these blessings and others, and averted from them calamities; and this obliges them to complete gratitude and remembrance of Him. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ because of their ignorance and wrongdoing. ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾: those who acknowledge the blessing of their Lord, humble themselves before Allah, love Him, and spend it in obedience to their Master and seeking His pleasure.

{62} ﴿That is﴾: the One who did what He did, ﴿Allah, your Lord﴾; that is, the One singled out for divinity and singled out for lordship, because His sole possession of these blessings is part of His lordship, and His making them obligate gratitude is part of His divinity. ﴿The Creator of all things﴾: an affirmation of His lordship. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾: an affirmation that He alone deserves worship, with no partner. Then He explicitly commanded worshipping Him, saying: ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾; that is, how are you turned away from worshipping Him alone, with no partner, after He has made the proof clear to you and illuminated the path for you?

{63} ﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾; that is, as a punishment for their denial of Allah's signs and their transgression against His messengers, they are turned away from monotheism and sincerity, as the Most High said: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, they look at one another, [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not comprehend.﴾

{64} ﴿Allah is the One who made for you the earth as a place of settlement﴾; that is, stable and at rest, prepared for all your interests, enabling you to cultivate it, plant in it, build upon it, travel, and reside in it. ﴿And the sky as a canopy﴾: a ceiling over the earth on which you live, in which Allah placed what you benefit from in lights and signs by which one is guided in the darkness of land and sea. ﴿And He shaped you and perfected your forms﴾: there is no form more beautiful among the kinds of living creatures than the children of Adam, as the Most High said: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾. If you wish to know the beauty of the human being and the perfection of Allah's wisdom in him, then look at him member by member: will you find any member of his that suits him and would be fit to be in another place? Look also at the affection in hearts for one another: will you find that among other than human beings? And look at what Allah has specially bestowed upon him: intellect, faith, love, and knowledge, which are the finest morals, befitting the most beautiful forms. ﴿And provided you with good things﴾: this includes every good thing of food, drink, marriage, clothing, sight, hearing, and other good things that Allah made easy for His servants, facilitated the means to them, and prohibited the corrupt things that oppose them and harm their bodies, hearts, and religions. ﴿That is﴾: the One who arranged affairs and bestowed these blessings upon you, ﴿Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾; that is, He is exalted, and His goodness and benevolence are abundant, the Sustainer of all the worlds through His blessings.

{65} ﴿He is the Living﴾: the One who possesses complete and perfect life, entailing the essential attributes that His life cannot be complete without, such as hearing, sight, power, knowledge, speech, and other attributes of perfection and qualities of majesty. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾; that is, no one is worthy of worship except His noble Face. ﴿So invoke Him, [being] sincere to Him in religion﴾: this includes both the invocation of worship and the invocation of request. That is, direct every act of worship, supplication, and deed to the Face of Allah, for sincerity is what is commanded, as the Most High said: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining toward truth﴾. ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾; that is, all praises, commendations, and thanks, by speech such as the creatures' mention of Him, and by action such as their worship of Him. All of that belongs to Allah alone, with no partner, because of His perfection in His attributes and actions and the completeness of His blessings.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verse 69–76:

{69} {Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah?} – the clear and manifest signs – marveling at their abominable condition. {How are they turned away?}; that is: how do they turn away from them? And to what do they go after the complete clarification? Do they find clear signs that contradict the signs of Allah? No, by Allah. Or do they find dubious arguments that accord with their desires, and with which they assault (the truth) for the sake of their falsehood?

{70–72} Evil is what they have exchanged and chosen for themselves, by denying the Book that came to them from Allah and what Allah sent His messengers with – messengers who are the best of creation, the most truthful of them, and the greatest of them in intellect. For these people there is no recompense but the blazing Fire. Therefore Allah threatened them with its punishment, saying: {But they will come to know, when the shackles are around their necks}, which prevent them from any movement, {and the chains}, by which they and their devils are linked together, {they will be dragged – In scalding water}; that is, water whose boiling and heat has intensified. {Then in the Fire they will be set ablaze}: the great flame will be kindled upon them, so they will be burned by it. Then they will be rebuked for their polytheism and their lying.

{73–74} And it will be said to them: {Where is what you used to associate with Allah – besides Allah?} Did they benefit you, or did they ward off from you some of the punishment? {They will say: They have strayed from us}; that is, they have vanished and are not present. And even if they were present, they would not benefit. Then they denied, saying: {Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before}. It is possible that their intention by this is denial, and they thought it would benefit and avail them. And it is possible – and this is the more apparent – that their intention by this is an acknowledgment of the falsehood of the divinity of what they used to worship, and that there is no partner with Allah in reality, and that they were merely astray and mistaken in worshipping something that has no divinity. This is indicated by His saying: {Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers}; that is, such is the misguidance they were upon in the world – a misguidance evident to everyone, to the extent that they themselves acknowledge its falsehood on the Day of Resurrection. And the meaning of His saying becomes clear to them: {And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners; they follow only assumption}, and it is indicated by His saying: {And on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association}, {And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection...} – the verses.

{75} It will be said to the people of the Fire: {That is} – the punishment that has been apportioned to you – {because you used to exult in the earth without right and because you used to be insolent}; that is, you used to exult in the falsehood you were upon, and in the knowledge by which you opposed the knowledge of the messengers, and you were insolent toward the servants of Allah, out of transgression, aggression, injustice, and disobedience. As He said at the end of this surah: {So when their messengers came to them with clear evidences, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had}, and as the people of Qarun said to him: {Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant}. This is the blameworthy exultation that necessitates punishment, unlike the praiseworthy exultation about which Allah said: {Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy – in that let them rejoice}, which is exultation in beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds.

{76} {Enter the gates of Hell}, each into a level of its levels according to the measure of his deeds, {abiding therein}, never to leave it. {Wretched is the abode of the arrogant}: an abode in which they will be disgraced, humiliated, confined, and punished, oscillating between its heat and its bitter cold.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verse 78:

So the demand of the one who demands from the messengers the bringing of signs is injustice on their part, obstinacy, and denial after Allah had supported them with the signs indicating their truthfulness and the soundness of what they brought. {But when the command of Allah comes}: with the decision between the messengers and their enemies, and the victory, {it will be judged}: between them {with truth}: that which falls in its proper place and accords with what is correct, by saving the messengers and their followers and destroying the deniers. Therefore He said: {And the falsifiers will lose there}; that is, at the time of the judgment mentioned, {those the description of whom is falsehood}, and what they brought of knowledge and action is falsehood, and their ultimate aim for themselves is falsehood. So let these addressees beware of continuing in their falsehood, lest they lose as those lost; for these are no better than them, and they have no exemption in the books for salvation.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 79–81:

{79–80} Allah bestows His favour upon His servants through the livestock He has made for them, which contain a great many blessings. Among them are the benefits of riding upon them and carrying loads; the benefits of eating their meat and drinking their milk; and [the benefits of] warmth, and of making implements and household goods from their wool, their fleece, and their hair ... and other benefits besides. ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts﴾: [this refers to] reaching distant lands, and gaining joy and delight in them, and being welcomed with gladness by their people. ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾; that is, upon the land-riding beasts and the sea-going ships, Allah carries you, He who subjected them and prepared for them the causes He prepared, which cannot be completed without them.

{81} ﴿And He shows you His signs﴾: those which point to His oneness and to His names and attributes. This is among His greatest blessings, for He lets His servants witness His signs within themselves and His signs on the horizons, and His manifest blessings, and enumerates them for them, so that they may know Him, thank Him, and remember Him. ﴿So which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾; that is, which one of His signs do you not acknowledge? For it is established among you that all signs and blessings come from Him, the Exalted, so there remains no place for denial, nor any room for turning away from them. Rather, they make it obligatory upon people of understanding to exert their utmost effort and expend their full capacity in striving to obey Him, devoting themselves to His service and turning wholly to Him.

For it is established among you that all signs and blessings come from Him, the Exalted, so there remains no place for denial, nor any room for turning away from them. Rather, they make it obligatory upon people of understanding to exert their utmost effort and expend their full capacity in striving to obey Him, devoting themselves to His service and turning wholly to Him.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 79–81:

{79–80} Allah bestows His favour upon His servants through the livestock He has made for them, which contain a great many blessings. Among them are the benefits of riding upon them and carrying loads; the benefits of eating their meat and drinking their milk; and [the benefits of] warmth, and of making implements and household goods from their wool, their fleece, and their hair ... and other benefits besides. ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts﴾: [this refers to] reaching distant lands, and gaining joy and delight in them, and being welcomed with gladness by their people. ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾; that is, upon the land-riding beasts and the sea-going ships, Allah carries you, He who subjected them and prepared for them the causes He prepared, which cannot be completed without them.

{81} ﴿And He shows you His signs﴾: those which point to His oneness and to His names and attributes. This is among His greatest blessings, for He lets His servants witness His signs within themselves and His signs on the horizons, and His manifest blessings, and enumerates them for them, so that they may know Him, thank Him, and remember Him. ﴿So which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾; that is, which one of His signs do you not acknowledge? For it is established among you that all signs and blessings come from Him, the Exalted, so there remains no place for denial, nor any room for turning away from them. Rather, they make it obligatory upon people of understanding to exert their utmost effort and expend their full capacity in striving to obey Him, devoting themselves to His service and turning wholly to Him.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 40, verses 82–85:

{82} Exalted is He, urges those who denied His Messenger to travel through the earth with their bodies and their hearts, and to ask the people of knowledge, {so that they may look}: a look of reflection and inference, not a look of heedlessness and neglect, {at how was the end of those before them}: from the past nations, such as ʿAd, Thamud and others who were greater than them in strength, more abundant in wealth, and more lasting in traces upon the earth, in fortified buildings, elegant gardens and abundant crops. {Then what they used to earn did not avail them}: when the command of Allah came upon them. Their strength did not avail them, they could not ransom themselves with their wealth, and they were not protected by their fortresses.

{83} Then he mentioned their great crime, saying: {When their messengers came to them with clear proofs}: from the divine books, the great miracles, and beneficial knowledge that clarifies guidance from error and truth from falsehood, {they rejoiced in what knowledge they had}: which contradicted the religion of the messengers. It is well known that their rejoicing in it indicates their intense satisfaction with it, their adherence to it, and their hostility toward the truth the messengers brought, and their making falsehood appear as truth. This is general to all the sciences by which what the messengers brought was contradicted. Among the most deserving of entering into this are the sciences of philosophy and Greek logic, by which many verses of the Qur'an have been rejected, which have diminished its status in hearts, and which have made its certain, decisive proofs into mere verbal proofs that yield no certainty at all, while the intellects of the foolish and the false are preferred over it. This is among the greatest forms of blasphemy against the signs of Allah, of opposing them and contradicting them; so Allah is the One sought for help. {And there descended upon them}; i.e., there came down what they used to mock: the punishment.

{84} {So when they saw Our might}; i.e., Our punishment, they acknowledged, at a time when acknowledgment would not benefit them, and {said: "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him"}: the idols and images, and they disowned everything that opposed the messengers, whether in knowledge or in action.

{85} {So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might}; i.e., in that state. This is {the way of Allah} and His custom {which has passed among His servants}: that when the might and punishment of Allah descend upon the deniers, their faith, if they believe, is not valid and does not save them from the punishment. That is because it is the faith of necessity, which they were compelled to, and the faith of witnessing. The beneficial faith that saves its possessor is the voluntary faith that is belief in the unseen, and that is before the signs of punishment appear. {And there the disbelievers lost}; i.e., at the time of destruction and the tasting of might, {their religion, their worldly life, and their hereafter}. It is not sufficient merely to lose in that abode; rather there must be a loss that brings wretchedness in severe punishment, and abiding in it forever and ever.

Here ends the commentary on Surah Al-Mu'min, by the praise, kindness and help of Allah, not by our own power and strength. To Him belongs thanks and praise.
